The offering the author makes at the end of his essay likewise goes no further than a few phrases from the imperial instructions, yet his loyalty and affection are conveyed with exquisite sincerity. I have hopes that you will one day deliver lectures at the Classics Colloquium.〕

Comment by Associate Examiner Zou, Instructor

〔The book Method of the Mind is the means by which Emperor Wen carried forward the learning of the sages and transmitted it to his sagely sons and divine grandsons, to inaugurate great peace for ten thousand generations. Its broad outlines and essential purport are set forth with great clarity and detail in the imperially composed preface. As for the maxims of the sages and worthies of former times, these too are fully recorded in its four juan. The intention of the examination authorities today is merely to expound and proclaim…〕

title: 正德八年河南鄉試錄
text:
聖謨以仰裨
聖德而塲中荅者乃茫無所知篇終之獻往往別爲一說徐而觀之皆老生之常談耳此策不
然其能服膺
祖訓者歟
考試官學正王　批　敬
天法
祖勤政用人謹好惡辨邪正明賞罰繼世而有天下者脩德保位之大端也
故
文皇於心法序中必兢天心人心君心言之此策能悉以陳而謂
===
今日之所要者急者在是可謂能仰識
聖心者矣錄之庶有所藉以達于吾
聖天子
考試官教授陸　批　於
聖製中及心字者敷陳蓋矣非留心
聖學之士何能如此
帝王之治出於道而道不外乎心帝王之
學原於心而心不離乎道蓋道者治之本
也必心以爲之歸宿外乎心則治不出於
punctuated:
聖謨，以仰裨聖德。而塲中荅者乃茫無所知，篇終之獻往往別爲一說，徐而觀之，皆老生之常談耳。此策不然，其能服膺祖訓者歟？
考試官學正王批：敬天、法祖、勤政、用人、謹好惡、辨邪正、明賞罰，繼世而有天下者脩德保位之大端也。故文皇於《心法》序中必兢天心、人心、君心言之。此策能悉以陳，而謂今日之所要者、急者在是，可謂能仰識聖心者矣。錄之，庶有所藉以達于吾聖天子。
考試官教授陸批：於聖製中及心字者，敷陳蓋矣。非留心聖學之士，何能如此？
帝王之治出於道，而道不外乎心；帝王之學原於心，而心不離乎道。蓋道者，治之本也，必心以爲之歸宿。外乎心，則治不出於
translation_en:
…the imperial counsels, thereby assisting the cultivation of imperial virtue. Yet those answering in the examination hall knew nothing of this. The recommendations at the ends of their essays often advanced some separate argument; examined at leisure, they proved to be nothing but stale commonplaces. This policy essay is different. Is its author someone who has truly taken the ancestral instructions to heart?
Comment by Examiner Wang, Instructor: Revering Heaven, emulating the ancestors, attending diligently to government, employing worthy men, exercising care in one's likes and dislikes, distinguishing the wicked from the upright, and making rewards and punishments clear—these are the chief means by which a ruler who inherits the realm cultivates virtue and secures his throne. Thus, in his preface to Methods of the Mind, Emperor Wen necessarily speaks with reverent concern [?] of the mind of Heaven, the minds of the people, and the mind of the ruler. This policy essay sets all these matters forth and declares that they constitute what is essential and urgent today. Its author may indeed be said to understand the imperial mind. We record it in the hope that this may provide a means for it to reach our sagely Son of Heaven.
Comment by Examiner Lu, Professor: The passages in the imperial composition that mention the word “mind” have been fully expounded [?]. How could anyone accomplish this without devoting himself to the learning of the sages?
The government of emperors and kings proceeds from the Way, and the Way does not lie outside the mind; the learning of emperors and kings originates in the mind, and the mind is inseparable from the Way. For the Way is the foundation of government, and it must find its ultimate resting place in the mind. Apart from the mind, government does not proceed from…

title: 正德八年河南鄉試錄
text:
道矣心者學之源也必道以爲之主宰離
乎道則學不原於心矣治不出於道既無
其本雖有小小之補塞不足以稱治學不
原於心既無其源雖極區區之探討不足
以成學此我
太宗文皇帝聖學心法一書之所由輯而有以
繼往聖之絕學以開
今日之盛治也愚嘗伏讀
高皇聖諭有曰帝王莫盛於堯舜然觀其授受
===
在允執厥中
文皇聖諭亦曰堯舜相傳允執厥中便足爲治
大哉
王言一哉
王心舜之所受於堯而益之三言以授禹者心
法首載之矣豈非即我
祖宗之所爲授受者歟是書所集皆聖賢之言
文皇自謂於正心脩身齊家治國平天下之要
道大畧已見其于孔氏之書微詞奧旨類
punctuated:
道矣。心者，學之源也，必道以爲之主宰；離乎道，則學不原於心矣。治不出於道，既無其本，雖有小小之補塞，不足以稱治；學不原於心，既無其源，雖極區區之探討，不足以成學。此我太宗文皇帝《聖學心法》一書之所由輯，而有以繼往聖之絕學，以開今日之盛治也。
愚嘗伏讀高皇聖諭，有曰：「帝王莫盛於堯舜，然觀其授受，在允執厥中。」文皇聖諭亦曰：「堯舜相傳，允執厥中，便足爲治。」大哉，王言！一哉，王心！舜之所受於堯，而益之三言以授禹者，《心法》首載之矣。豈非即我祖宗之所爲授受者歟？
是書所集，皆聖賢之言。文皇自謂：「於正心、脩身、齊家、治國、平天下之要道，大畧已見。」其于孔氏之書，微詞奧旨，類
translation_en:
…the Way. The mind is the source of learning, and the Way must govern it; apart from the Way, learning does not originate in the mind. When government does not proceed from the Way, it lacks its root: even small repairs and remedies do not suffice to merit the name of government. When learning does not originate in the mind, it lacks its source: even the most painstaking pursuit of petty inquiries does not suffice to constitute learning. This is why our Emperor Taizong Wen compiled the book Essential Methods of the Mind in Sagely Learning (Shengxue xinfa): thereby to carry forward the interrupted learning of the sages of the past and inaugurate the flourishing government of today.
I have reverently read Emperor Gao’s sacred instructions, which say: “Among emperors and kings, none surpassed Yao and Shun. Yet when we examine what they transmitted and received, it lay in ‘Sincerely hold fast to the Mean.’” Emperor Wen’s sacred instructions likewise say: “What Yao and Shun transmitted to one another—‘Sincerely hold fast to the Mean’—was sufficient for governing.” How great are these royal words! How united are these royal minds! What Shun received from Yao, and augmented with three further sayings to transmit to Yu, is recorded at the beginning of Essential Methods of the Mind. Is this not precisely what our imperial ancestors transmitted and received?
Everything collected in this book consists of the words of sages and worthies. Emperor Wen himself stated: “The essential Way of rectifying the mind, cultivating oneself, regulating the family, governing the state, and bringing peace to all under Heaven is already broadly set forth.” As for the subtle expressions and profound meanings in the writings of Confucius, generally …

title: 正德八年河南鄉試錄
text:
從來錄統言專言之間綱提目舉寧復有
遺憾乎今
御製序文具在序括諸篇篇爲之釋事必求道
言必原心論天而必反諸躬取人而必考
諸已丹青炳煥歷世弗渝雲漢昭回有目
同仰所謂萬事根於一心先明諸心使無
毫髮之蔽裁制萬物各得其宜則體周用
備者首是書之旨也所謂天命無常惟德
是與惟能脩德以合天心則天命眷顧久
===
而益隆者終是書之意也而又謂人心之
敬怠有間天命之去留無常者序敬天也
祖宗之法以爲後世當敬守之不可以忽
者序法祖也一心之用周流天地德以服
人宜莫如勤者序勤政也一人之心有好
惡衆人之議合至公者序用人也序謹好
惡則有心之好惡不可不慎苟爲不慎蔽
固溺深之儆序辯邪正則有明君之心公
以正君子之心有所合而偏邪之人無自
punctuated: 從來錄統言專言之間，綱提目舉，寧復有遺憾乎？今御製序文具在，序括諸篇，篇爲之釋。事必求道，言必原心；論天而必反諸躬，取人而必考諸已。丹青炳煥，歷世弗渝；雲漢昭回，有目同仰。所謂「萬事根於一心，先明諸心，使無毫髮之蔽，裁制萬物，各得其宜，則體周用備」者，首是書之旨也。所謂「天命無常，惟德是與，惟能脩德以合天心，則天命眷顧久而益隆」者，終是書之意也。而又謂「人心之敬怠有間，天命之去留無常」者，序敬天也。「祖宗之法，以爲後世當敬守之，不可以忽」者，序法祖也。「一心之用，周流天地，德以服人，宜莫如勤」者，序勤政也。「一人之心有好惡，衆人之議合至公」者，序用人也。序謹好惡，則有「心之好惡不可不慎，苟爲不慎，蔽固溺深」之儆；序辯邪正，則有「明君之心公以正，君子之心有所合，而偏邪之人無自
translation_en: …collected and recorded [?], between comprehensive and particular statements, with the main principles presented and their particulars enumerated—could anything still be left wanting? Now the imperially composed preface remains available in full. The preface encompasses the several chapters, and the chapters explain it. In affairs, one must seek the Way; in words, one must trace their source to the mind. When discussing Heaven, one must turn back to examine oneself; when selecting others, one must test them against oneself. Brilliant as painted colors, it remains unchanged through successive ages; radiant as the Milky Way, it is admired by all who have eyes. Its statement that “the myriad affairs are rooted in a single mind; first make the mind clear, allowing not the slightest obscuration, and regulate the myriad things so that each attains what is fitting: then substance will be all-embracing and function complete” expresses the purpose with which this book begins. Its statement that “Heaven’s Mandate is not constant: it supports virtue alone; only by cultivating virtue to accord with Heaven’s mind can the favor of Heaven’s Mandate endure and grow ever greater” expresses the intent with which the book ends. Furthermore, the statement that “the human mind alternates between reverence and negligence, while the departure or continuance of Heaven’s Mandate is not constant” introduces the chapter on Revering Heaven. The statement that “the institutions of the ancestors should be reverently preserved by later generations and must not be neglected” introduces the chapter on Emulating the Ancestors. The statement that “the activity of a single mind circulates throughout Heaven and Earth; to win people’s submission through virtue, nothing is more fitting than diligence” introduces the chapter on Diligence in Government. The statement that “one person’s mind has its likes and dislikes, while the deliberations of the many accord with utmost impartiality” introduces the chapter on Employing Men. In introducing the chapter on Being Cautious in Likes and Dislikes, it warns that “one must exercise caution in the mind’s likes and dislikes; without caution, one becomes firmly blinded and deeply engulfed.” In introducing the chapter on Distinguishing the Perverse from the Upright, it states that “the enlightened ruler’s mind is impartial and upright, so the minds of gentlemen find something with which to accord, while partial and perverse men have no means of…”

title: 正德八年河南鄉試錄
text:
入之論序明賞罰則又有人君以天地爲
心則賞罰必當之說凡此皆所以原心而
求道者也而序之終篇又欲
聖子神孫觀是書者先觀其序以知其用心其
詞肯之丁寧誨諭之詳至舜禹而後實見
予今
列聖相承聿脩厥德誦服是書成憲以監古訓
有獲四方用靖萬邦作孚於萬斯年受天
之祐所以永
===
宗社之慶於悠久以無負
皇祖之訓者蓋世有哲王道此一道而心此一
心矣而執事尤以今日之要且急者爲問
豈不以敬
天法
祖勤政用人爲大且要而謹好惡辯邪正明賞
罰又其當急者乎
聖謨洋洋嘉言孔彰歛袵展卷日星在懸𦒿生
之常談愚豈容復贅而天下大器保之最
punctuated: 入之論。序明賞罰，則又有人君以天地爲心，則賞罰必當之說。凡此皆所以原心而求道者也。而序之終篇，又欲聖子神孫觀是書者，先觀其序，以知其用心。其詞肯之丁寧、誨諭之詳，至舜禹而後，實見予今。列聖相承，聿脩厥德，誦服是書，成憲以監，古訓有獲，四方用靖，萬邦作孚，於萬斯年受天之祐。所以永宗社之慶於悠久，以無負皇祖之訓者，蓋世有哲王，道此一道而心此一心矣。而執事尤以今日之要且急者爲問，豈不以敬天、法祖、勤政、用人爲大且要，而謹好惡、辯邪正、明賞罰，又其當急者乎？聖謨洋洋，嘉言孔彰，歛袵展卷，日星在懸。𦒿生之常談，愚豈容復贅？而天下大器，保之最
translation_en:
…the argument that they have no way to gain entry. In introducing the clarification of rewards and punishments, the preface further states that if the ruler takes Heaven and Earth as his own mind, rewards and punishments will necessarily be fitting. All these teachings seek the Way by examining the mind at its source. At its conclusion, the preface further wishes that the sage sons and divine grandsons who read this book should first read its preface, so as to understand the intentions behind it. The earnest insistence of its wording [?] and the thoroughness of its instruction and admonition have, since Shun and Yu, truly appeared again in our own day [?].

The successive sage emperors have carried on one another’s work and cultivated their virtue, reciting and putting into practice this book. They take established statutes as their guide and gain insight from ancient teachings. Thus the four quarters are pacified and the myriad states become trusting; for ten thousand years they receive Heaven’s protection. The means by which they perpetuate the blessings of the ancestral temples and the altars of soil and grain into the distant future, without failing the imperial ancestor’s instructions, is surely this: each age has its wise king, who follows this same Way and takes this same mind as his own.

Yet you, honored examiners, ask particularly about what is essential and urgent today. Is this not because revering Heaven, emulating the ancestors, attending diligently to government, and employing worthy men are matters of great and essential importance, while exercising care in one’s likes and dislikes, distinguishing the wicked from the upright, and making rewards and punishments clear are also matters requiring urgent attention? The sage counsels are abundant, and their excellent words shine brightly. Composing one’s robes respectfully and opening the volume, one sees them like the sun and stars hanging above. These are the familiar teachings of aged scholars; how could I, in my ignorance, presume to add more? Yet All-under-Heaven is a great vessel, and preserving it is most…

title: 正德八年河南鄉試錄
text:
難善保則完不善則壞欲不可縱心不可
侈以道制欲以理制心庶幾寡過之訓又
祖宗之所拳拳以致慎於將來者蓋治世之龜
鑑保邦之藥石草茅之賤倘荷收錄獲覲
于
聖天子
經筵之日願隨執事奉此以往謹對
第二問
張景
考試官學正王　批〔士之所以能自樹立者以此氣爾子知所以善養而且以不待於人爲決然之論固已可偉末篇集義知命之說又有得於孟氏心法之外者即其所充吾知其他日立〕
〔朝風采必有可以竦人者矣予其毋負主司者之深屬也哉〕
考試官教授陸　批〔文勢洶湧直欲推倒一時豪傑非經學䆮仗舉子所能及〕
氣之於人也大矣其善養之機由於已而
無所待於人者也夫氣吾氣也人之所同
得而本自浩然者失所養則至於自餒而
punctuated:
難。善保則完，不善則壞。欲不可縱，心不可侈；以道制欲，以理制心，庶幾寡過之訓，又祖宗之所拳拳以致慎於將來者。蓋治世之龜鑑，保邦之藥石。草茅之賤，倘荷收錄，獲覲于聖天子經筵之日，願隨執事奉此以往。謹對。

第二問
張景
考試官學正王，批〔士之所以能自樹立者，以此氣爾。子知所以善養，而且以不待於人爲決然之論，固已可偉。末篇集義知命之說，又有得於孟氏心法之外者。即其所充，吾知其他日立〕〔朝風采，必有可以竦人者矣。予其毋負主司者之深屬也哉！〕
考試官教授陸，批〔文勢洶湧，直欲推倒一時豪傑，非經學䆮仗舉子所能及。〕

氣之於人也大矣！其善養之機，由於已而無所待於人者也。夫氣，吾氣也，人之所同得而本自浩然者。失所養，則至於自餒而
translation_en:
…difficult. Preserve it well, and it remains whole; fail to do so, and it falls into ruin. Desires must not be indulged, nor must the mind grow extravagant. The instruction to regulate desires through the Way and restrain the mind through principle, thereby perhaps committing few errors, is also what the imperial ancestors earnestly stressed to encourage vigilance for the future. It is a mirror for governing the age and a healing remedy for preserving the state. If I, a humble man of the countryside, should graciously be selected and gain an audience with the sagely Son of Heaven on a day of the Classics Colloquium, I would wish to accompany you and present these teachings. Respectfully submitted in reply.

Second Question
Zhang Jing
Examiner Wang, School Instructor, comments: 〔What enables a scholar to establish himself is this vital energy, qi. You understand how to nourish it well and firmly argue that this does not depend upon others: this is already admirable. The discussion of accumulating righteousness and understanding one's allotted destiny in the final part also contains insights beyond Master Meng's teaching of the mind. Judging by the fullness you have achieved, I know that when you someday take your place〕〔at court, your bearing will surely inspire awe. May you not disappoint the chief examiner's profound expectations of you! [?]〕
Examiner Lu, Instructor, comments: 〔The force of the writing surges powerfully, as though intent on toppling all the outstanding men of the age. It is beyond the reach of examination candidates who rely on classical learning [?].〕

Great indeed is the importance of qi to human beings! The means of nourishing it well lies within oneself and does not depend upon others. This qi is our own qi, something all people alike receive and which is inherently vast and flowing. If it is not properly nourished, one eventually becomes inwardly depleted and…

title: 正德八年河南鄉試錄
text:
不能以自拔矣此善養之説所以爲聖賢
之大致而學者所當從事也易曰立天之
道曰陰與陽立地之道曰柔與剛立人之
道曰仁與義自夫陰陽剛柔仁義之説立
而世之言氣者異矣天地之間莫非此氣
動直者陽而動闢者剛而
時立者固剛也發舒者仁而□裂者固亦
仁也力之有強弱者氣稟之不齊養之皆
浩然者體段之本無異爾懦弱邪佞之病
===
固不可以語氣之充而況靜愿慤之質正
所以爲大勇之本也顧世之人歉於義者
不能以自奮而重於得喪者又不免待人
而興焉孟子曰無是餒也又曰豪傑之士
雖無文王猶興噫能知此者寡矣是亦何
惟吾夫子有未見剛者之嘆而孟子以善
養自許哉但其一時問答之詞非已矣之
絶嘆而學者於此自當有以求其實而取
則之也即孔子觀之司寇之位方及七日
punctuated: 不能以自拔矣。此善養之説所以爲聖賢之大致，而學者所當從事也。《易》曰：「立天之道曰陰與陽，立地之道曰柔與剛，立人之道曰仁與義。」自夫陰陽剛柔仁義之説立，而世之言氣者異矣。天地之間，莫非此氣。動直者陽，而動闢者剛，而時立者固剛也；發舒者仁，而□裂者固亦仁也。力之有強弱者，氣稟之不齊；養之皆浩然者，體段之本無異爾。懦弱邪佞之病，固不可以語氣之充，而況靜愿慤之質，正所以爲大勇之本也。顧世之人歉於義者，不能以自奮，而重於得喪者，又不免待人而興焉。孟子曰：「無是，餒也。」又曰：「豪傑之士，雖無文王猶興。」噫！能知此者寡矣。是亦何惟吾夫子有未見剛者之嘆，而孟子以善養自許哉？但其一時問答之詞，非已矣之絶嘆，而學者於此自當有以求其實而取則之也。即孔子觀之，司寇之位方及七日
translation_en: …and cannot extricate themselves. This is why the teaching of properly nourishing qi is a central concern of sages and worthies, and something to which students must devote themselves. The Book of Changes says: “Establishing the Way of Heaven, they called it yin and yang; establishing the Way of Earth, they called it yielding and firm; establishing the Way of humanity, they called it benevolence and righteousness.” Once this teaching concerning yin and yang, yielding and firm, and benevolence and righteousness was established, people’s accounts of qi became divergent. Between Heaven and Earth, nothing is other than this qi. That which moves straight is yang; that which moves expansively is firmness; and that which stands at the proper time is certainly firmness [?]. That which unfolds is benevolence, and that which □ splits is certainly also benevolence [?]. Differences in strength arise from unequal endowments of qi; that all can nourish it to become vast and flowing follows from its fundamentally identical constitution. The failings of cowardice, perversity, and obsequiousness certainly cannot be spoken of as fullness of qi. Still more, a disposition of quietness, sincerity, and honesty is precisely the foundation of great courage. Yet people deficient in righteousness cannot rouse themselves, while those who attach importance to gain and loss inevitably depend on others to inspire them. Mengzi says: “Without this, it starves.” He also says: “Outstanding men arise even without King Wen.” Alas! Few can understand this. Why, then, did our Master lament that he had never seen a truly firm person, while Mengzi professed himself adept at nourishing qi [?]? These, however, were words spoken in particular exchanges, not despairing sighs that all was over. Students should therefore seek their substance and take them as a model. Consider Confucius: he had held the office of Minister of Justice for only seven days…

title: 正德八年河南鄉試錄
text:
而誅少正卯者不少逭夾谷之會魯盖岌
岌矣從容數語齊且謝過不暇此其氣何
如也顏子至明至健而爲邦之問毅然以
王者之事爲已任曾子唯一貫之速而弘
毅之力量尤不可以抑視他如子夏之謹
嚴子路之勇果固皆有以進乎是曾謂聖
門無剛者乎自夫子有剛之説而養氣之
論獨發於孟子觀其在賓師之位非齊王
所能臣而於公孫衍張儀輩直視之爲妾
===
婦其氣之充要亦無愧於孔子者當時如
告子樂正子之流咸得其一偏而望迹如
魯仲連者亦庶幾矣秦漢而下此風泯泯
間有能存者雖不敢望孔孟之轍差亦足
以扶衰救敝抑邪伸正是皆可與者焉茹
芝如四皓卒能成輔翼之功擊楫如祖逖
猶足發中原之憤一揖而去不克而死其
氣固浩然矣它如李膺諸君子之風節而
漢脉之一綫猶繫楊宏中輩之抗言剴切
punctuated: 而誅少正卯者不少逭。夾谷之會，魯盖岌岌矣，從容數語，齊且謝過不暇，此其氣何如也？顏子至明至健，而爲邦之問，毅然以王者之事爲已任。曾子唯一貫之速，而弘毅之力量，尤不可以抑視。他如子夏之謹嚴、子路之勇果，固皆有以進乎是，曾謂聖門無剛者乎？自夫子有剛之説，而養氣之論獨發於孟子。觀其在賓師之位，非齊王所能臣，而於公孫衍、張儀輩，直視之爲妾婦。其氣之充，要亦無愧於孔子者。當時如告子、樂正子之流，咸得其一偏，而望迹如魯仲連者，亦庶幾矣。秦漢而下，此風泯泯，間有能存者，雖不敢望孔孟之轍，差亦足以扶衰救敝、抑邪伸正，是皆可與者焉。茹芝如四皓，卒能成輔翼之功；擊楫如祖逖，猶足發中原之憤。一揖而去，不克而死，其氣固浩然矣。它如李膺諸君子之風節，而漢脉之一綫猶繫；楊宏中輩之抗言剴切，
translation_en:
…and, in executing Shaozheng Mao, he allowed not the slightest reprieve. At the meeting at Jiagu, Lu was indeed in a precarious position; yet with a few calmly spoken words, he left Qi scarcely able to apologize quickly enough. What must his vital force have been like! Master Yan possessed the utmost clarity and strength; when he asked about governing a state, he resolutely took the work of a true king as his own responsibility. Master Zeng was quick to grasp the single thread running through the teaching [?], and the strength of his broad-minded resolve especially must not be underestimated. Others, such as Zixia in his scrupulous seriousness and Zilu in his courage and decisiveness, certainly all made progress toward this. Could one possibly say that there were no men of firmness in the sage’s school?

Although the Master had spoken of firmness, it was Mencius alone who developed the discussion of nourishing vital force. Consider him in his position as an honored guest and teacher: even the king of Qi could not make him his subject. As for men like Gongsun Yan and Zhang Yi, he regarded them simply as concubines and wives. In the fullness of his vital force, he surely did not fall short of Confucius. Contemporaries such as Gaozi and Yuezhengzi each grasped one aspect of it; and someone like Lu Zhonglian, who aspired to follow in his footsteps, also came close.

From the Qin and Han onward, this spirit faded. Occasionally there were those who could preserve it. Though they could not presume to follow in the tracks of Confucius and Mencius, they were still sufficiently capable of supporting what was declining, remedying abuses, restraining the perverse, and upholding the upright. All these deserve approval. The Four Hoary Elders, who fed on mushrooms, ultimately rendered service as supporting wings; Zu Ti, who struck his oar, could still give expression to indignation over the Central Plain. To depart with a single bow, or to die without achieving victory—their vital force was assuredly vast and flowing. There were also the integrity and steadfastness of Li Ying and the other gentlemen, through whom the Han’s thread of life still held; and the forceful remonstrances of Yang Hongzhong and his companions, incisive and earnest…

title: 正德八年河南鄉試錄
text:
而當時之奸惡以暴彼豈虞成夫黨錮之
變而求名於編管之禍者哉亦其氣之浩
然而若是焉耳甚矣夫此氣之在人不可
不養也苟以其爲不足以集事而不待養
邪則夫孔孟之爲何往而非氣之充者苟
以其爲有所興起而後可邪則夫士之幼
學壯行者果何事而必待上之人成之春
秋戰國之世亦有作孔孟之氣者在于其
上乎揚子曰周之士也貴秦之士也賤此
===
蓋論世變之說而張子所謂剛則不回柔
則不立者固學者之明戒也學者知所以
自立則無不可爲之事而其所養也充矣
雖然氣之所以充者其功何如也始於義
之能集而有以伸吾之氣終於命之能知
而不沮喪於趨舍進退之正夫然後能以
自立有不待人而興起矣夫士之所以自
任者固宜知此而愚生所論亦惟爲士言
之爾爲人上者顧可聽其自至而不思所
punctuated:
而當時之奸惡以暴。彼豈虞成夫黨錮之變而求名於編管之禍者哉？亦其氣之浩然而若是焉耳。甚矣夫，此氣之在人不可不養也！苟以其爲不足以集事而不待養邪，則夫孔孟之爲，何往而非氣之充者？苟以其爲有所興起而後可邪，則夫士之幼學壯行者，果何事而必待上之人成之？春秋戰國之世，亦有作孔孟之氣者在于其上乎？揚子曰：「周之士也貴，秦之士也賤。」此蓋論世變之說，而張子所謂「剛則不回，柔則不立」者，固學者之明戒也。學者知所以自立，則無不可爲之事，而其所養也充矣。

雖然，氣之所以充者，其功何如也？始於義之能集，而有以伸吾之氣；終於命之能知，而不沮喪於趨舍進退之正。夫然後能以自立，有不待人而興起矣。夫士之所以自任者，固宜知此，而愚生所論，亦惟爲士言之爾。爲人上者，顧可聽其自至而不思所
translation_en:
…and the wickedness of those in power at the time was thereby exposed. Could those men have anticipated bringing about the disaster of the partisan prohibitions, or sought fame through the calamity of supervised exile? It was simply the vastness of their moral spirit that made them act thus. How essential it is that this spirit within people be nurtured! If one supposes that it is insufficient to accomplish affairs and therefore need not be nurtured, then where, in anything Confucius and Mencius did, was the fullness of this spirit absent? If one supposes that it can flourish only after receiving some external stimulus, then why must scholars, who study in youth and put their learning into practice in maturity, wait for those above them to bring their endeavors to fruition? In the Spring and Autumn and Warring States periods, was there anyone above Confucius and Mencius who stirred their spirit into activity? Master Yang said: “The scholars of Zhou were honored; the scholars of Qin were despised.” This is surely a statement about changes in the times. Master Zhang’s saying, “The firm do not bend; the yielding cannot stand,” is indeed a clear admonition to students. When students understand how to establish themselves, there is nothing they cannot undertake, and the spirit they nurture becomes full.

Nevertheless, what effort is required to bring this spirit to fullness? It begins with accumulating righteousness, thereby giving scope to one’s spirit; it culminates in understanding Heaven’s mandate, so that one does not lose heart in rightly choosing what to pursue or forgo, when to advance or withdraw. Only then can one establish oneself and rise to action without waiting for others. Scholars should certainly understand this as the basis for the responsibilities they take upon themselves. What I, an unworthy student, have argued has likewise been addressed solely to scholars. Yet may those who stand above others simply leave them to reach this point on their own, without considering how …

title: 正德八年河南鄉試錄
text:
以振之乎蓋不有以礪天下之銳則無以
伸天下之氣不有以伸天下之氣則無以
絶天下之倖是故人主以名驅人而以義
激之使天下皆相率以售其直嗚呼是惟
受人之所畏而不甘人之所喜者能之敢
以是爲明問復
第三問
李濂
同考試官訓導秦　批〔記誦多失本真答問不相對〕
〔值策場之通弊也此策爲場中最優者故取置前列〕
===
同考試官教諭桑　批〔衆言必折諸聖賢人必於其論〕
〔世古今聽言觀人之法也是作得之〕
考試官學正王　批〔韓周二子人皆知之至其所以爲優〕
〔劣者則皆未之深考而莫知所適從此篇辨析二子立言之當否者明白瑩〕
〔詳一本於理未復槩其爲人而直著其造詣淺深之實以爲立言之本非深有〕
〔所見不能也〕
考試官教授陸　批〔造詣精當見理分明非聽他人之間〕
〔而從旁竊記者〕
punctuated:
以振之乎？蓋不有以礪天下之銳，則無以伸天下之氣；不有以伸天下之氣，則無以絶天下之倖。是故人主以名驅人，而以義激之，使天下皆相率以售其直。嗚呼！是惟受人之所畏，而不甘人之所喜者能之。敢以是爲明問復。

第三問
李濂

同考試官訓導秦　批〔記誦多失本真，答問不相對，〕〔值策場之通弊也。此策爲場中最優者，故取置前列。〕

同考試官教諭桑　批〔衆言必折諸聖賢，人必於其論〕〔世，古今聽言觀人之法也。是作得之。〕

考試官學正王　批〔韓周二子，人皆知之；至其所以爲優〕〔劣者，則皆未之深考，而莫知所適從。此篇辨析二子立言之當否者，明白瑩〕〔詳，一本於理。未復槩其爲人，而直著其造詣淺深之實，以爲立言之本，非深有〕〔所見不能也。〕

考試官教授陸　批〔造詣精當，見理分明，非聽他人之間〕〔而從旁竊記者。〕
translation_en:
…how to rouse them? Unless the keen resolve of all under Heaven is sharpened, their vital spirit cannot be given full scope; unless their vital spirit is given full scope, their pursuit of undeserved advantage cannot be ended. Thus the ruler impels people through reputation and inspires them through righteousness, so that all under Heaven lead one another in bringing their integrity into service. Ah! Only one who accepts what others fear and takes no delight in what others enjoy can accomplish this. I venture to offer this in reply to your illuminating question.

Third Question
Li Lian

Comment by Associate Examiner Qin, Assistant Instructor: “Reliance on memorization often loses the original meaning, and answers fail to address the questions: these are common faults encountered in the policy-essay examination [?]. This policy essay is the best in this examination, and therefore has been selected and placed among the leading pieces.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Sang, Instructor: “All statements must be judged against the sages and worthies, and people must be considered in relation to their times [?]. This is the method, ancient and modern, for assessing statements and evaluating people. This composition has grasped it.”

Comment by Examiner Wang, Director of Studies: “Everyone knows the two masters Han and Zhou. Yet as to what makes one superior or inferior, people have not examined the matter deeply and do not know whom to follow. This essay distinguishes clearly and lucidly, and in detail, whether the two masters’ pronouncements are sound, grounding everything in principle. It does not proceed to generalize about their characters [?], but directly reveals the actual depth or shallowness of their attainments as the foundation of their pronouncements. This could not be achieved without profound insight.”

Comment by Examiner Lu, Professor: “The author’s attainments are refined and sound, and his understanding of principle is clear. This is not the work of someone who has listened to others’ words [?] and surreptitiously jotted them down from the sidelines.”

title: 正德八年河南鄉試錄
text:
聽言者必揆諸理而後可以爲折衷之準
觀人者必論其世而後可以盡儗倫之公
夫疑似之說不可以易辯而優劣之實不
可以輕議也即言而儗人者不以理揆固
無所據以爲是非之決不以世論亦何所
徵以極知言之道也哉執事發策及於周
韓二子而欲得其所以爲從違者承學生
晩而敢輕爲之說邪惟知言之功爲格致
之始事而尚友之道又取正之大端恭承
===
之下則亦不能以默無所請矣韓子起於
八代文衰之後其所著原道讀荀等篇皆
欲以明乎道者其言曰孟氏醇乎醇者也
又曰荀與揚也擇焉而不精語焉而不詳
夫自孟氏沒道學不傳而尊孟氏之說者
甚鮮愈獨出而尊信之可謂難矣程子謂
其千餘年後斷得分明者正謂此爾周子
生於千載道喪之時特作太極一圖正所
以啓夫學者其圖之說曰無極而太極又
punctuated:
聽言者必揆諸理，而後可以爲折衷之準；觀人者必論其世，而後可以盡儗倫之公。夫疑似之說不可以易辯，而優劣之實不可以輕議也。即言而儗人者，不以理揆，固無所據以爲是非之決；不以世論，亦何所徵以極知言之道也哉？執事發策及於周韓二子，而欲得其所以爲從違者，承學生晩，而敢輕爲之說邪？惟知言之功爲格致之始事，而尚友之道又取正之大端，恭承之下，則亦不能以默無所請矣。
韓子起於八代文衰之後，其所著《原道》《讀荀》等篇，皆欲以明乎道者。其言曰：「孟氏醇乎醇者也。」又曰：「荀與揚也，擇焉而不精，語焉而不詳。」夫自孟氏沒，道學不傳，而尊孟氏之說者甚鮮，愈獨出而尊信之，可謂難矣。程子謂其千餘年後斷得分明者，正謂此爾。
周子生於千載道喪之時，特作太極一圖，正所以啓夫學者。其圖之說曰：「無極而太極。」又
translation_en:
Those who listen to statements must weigh them against principle before they can establish a standard for sound judgment; those who assess people must consider the age in which they lived before they can be wholly fair in comparing them. Plausible but doubtful doctrines cannot be readily distinguished, and actual superiority or inferiority cannot be lightly judged. When comparing people on the basis of their statements, without weighing these against principle one certainly has no basis for deciding right and wrong; without considering their times, what evidence could one draw upon to master the way of understanding statements? Your policy question addresses the two masters, Zhou and Han, seeking the grounds for accepting or rejecting their views. Born late and still a student, how could I venture lightly to pronounce upon them? Yet the work of understanding statements is the first step in investigating things and extending knowledge, while seeking friendship with the worthy of antiquity is a principal means of finding guidance toward what is correct. Having respectfully received your question, I therefore cannot remain silent without submitting my views.
Master Han arose after literary writing had declined through eight dynasties. His essays, including Inquiry into the Way (Yuan Dao) and Reading Xunzi (Du Xun), all sought to elucidate the Way. He said: “Master Meng was purest of the pure.” He also said: “Xun and Yang made their selections without precision and expressed themselves without thoroughness.” After Master Meng died, learning concerning the Way ceased to be transmitted, and very few honored his teachings. That Han Yu alone stepped forward to honor and trust them was truly difficult. This is precisely what Master Cheng meant when he said that, more than a thousand years later, Han had reached a clear judgment.
Master Zhou lived at a time when the Way had been lost for a thousand years. He expressly produced a Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate to enlighten students. His explanation of the diagram says: “Without Ultimate, yet the Supreme Ultimate.” And further …

title: 正德八年河南鄉試錄
text:
曰太極本無極夫自孔子有太極之說未
有言無極者而周子獨得而指言之可謂
精矣朱子謂其不由師傳默契道體者正
謂是爾夫即韓子之說固亦若有所得而
傑出於諸家者但其以學文爲第一義則
不免於牽制詞章之習而周子之學性諸
天成諸己上接洙泗千載之統下啓河洛
百世之傳固非韓之所得而並矣或乃疑
其言之相當而無所於從違彼固未揆諸
===
理而槩視之爾原道以博愛爲仁不免遺
體而通書之所謂愛曰仁者蓋别其用而
因以名體也於大學言誠意正心而不及
致知格物是爲無本而通書所謂守之貴
行之利者蓋承仁義中正而言本末之序
亦明矣人性本無不善原性分以爲三品
其說固差彼剛柔善惡中之說則指氣禀
而反之者言此豈愈之所能識也鬼神不
過一氣原鬼以土石風霆與之對言尤爲
punctuated: 曰：「太極本無極。」夫自孔子有太極之說，未有言無極者，而周子獨得而指言之，可謂精矣。朱子謂其不由師傳、默契道體者，正謂是爾。夫即韓子之說，固亦若有所得而傑出於諸家者，但其以學文爲第一義，則不免於牽制詞章之習。而周子之學，性諸天，成諸己，上接洙泗千載之統，下啓河洛百世之傳，固非韓之所得而並矣。或乃疑其言之相當，而無所於從違，彼固未揆諸理而槩視之爾。《原道》以博愛爲仁，不免遺體，而《通書》之所謂「愛曰仁」者，蓋别其用而因以名體也。於《大學》言誠意正心，而不及致知格物，是爲無本；而《通書》所謂「守之貴，行之利」者，蓋承仁義中正而言，本末之序亦明矣。人性本無不善，《原性》分以爲三品，其說固差；彼剛柔善惡中之說，則指氣禀而反之者言，此豈愈之所能識也？鬼神不過一氣，《原鬼》以土石風霆與之對言，尤爲
translation_en:
…says: “The Supreme Ultimate is fundamentally without ultimate.” Since Confucius propounded the Supreme Ultimate, no one had spoken of the ‘without ultimate’; Master Zhou alone grasped it and explicitly identified it. His insight may indeed be called profound. This is precisely what Master Zhu meant when he said that Zhou, without receiving instruction from a teacher, tacitly accorded with the substance of the Way. Master Han’s explanations, too, certainly seem to show some understanding that distinguishes him among the various thinkers. Yet because he made literary study his foremost concern, he could not escape being constrained by the habits of literary composition. Master Zhou’s learning, however, was endowed by Heaven and perfected in himself. Reaching back, it continued the thousand-year succession from the Zhu and Si rivers; reaching forward, it opened the transmission of the He and Luo rivers for a hundred generations. Han’s attainments certainly cannot be placed on a par with these. Some nevertheless wonder whether their statements are equivalent and cannot decide which to accept or reject. They have simply viewed them indiscriminately without measuring them against principle.
In Inquiry into the Way, Han defines benevolence as universal love, thereby failing to account fully for its substance. The statement in the Book of Penetration that “love is called benevolence,” however, distinguishes its function and thereby names its substance. In discussing the Great Learning, Han speaks of making the intentions sincere and rectifying the mind, but does not address extending knowledge and investigating things. This leaves his account without a foundation. By contrast, the Book of Penetration’s statement that “to preserve it is noble; to practice it is beneficial” follows upon its discussion of benevolence, righteousness, centrality, and correctness, so that the ordering of root and branches is also clear. Human nature is originally without anything that is not good. Inquiry into Human Nature divides it into three grades: its explanation is certainly mistaken. Zhou’s account of firmness, softness, goodness, evil, and the mean, however, refers to one’s endowment of vital energy and the means of returning from it to one’s original nature. How could Han Yu have understood this? Ghosts and spirits are nothing more than the single vital energy. Inquiry into Ghosts sets earth, stone, wind, and thunder in opposition to them, which is especially…

title: 正德八年河南鄉試錄
text:
不經彼神妙萬物之說則以不滯於有無
而論此豈愈之所能知也蓋愈之資才甚
高而因文見道是以無窮究精察之實而
周子之書不盡言圖不盡意蓋脉絡分明
而規模宏遠矣是其優劣固不待辨而謂
其言之大畧相當者不已過乎執事猶以
爲所優者乃在於人而不在於言夫即其
言而考其行韓子之爲人也其平居則不
過酣飲博奕之樂其自負則止惟功名進
===
取之念其排佛老之功未有而於潮州之
竄寞乃遂變其處禍福死生之際若謝潮
州表及張籍侑奠之詞則有愧於異學之
流甚多是其見道不精而徒用力於言語
文字之間者矣周子聞道甚早信古好義
胷次洒落而光風霽月之趣可挹遇事剛
果而玉色金聲之著尤毅其家甚約而其
意甚適其取名甚短而希世徼福之念甚
薄蓋其析之有以極其精而不亂合之有
punctuated:
不經。彼神妙萬物之說，則以不滯於有無而論，此豈愈之所能知也？蓋愈之資才甚高，而因文見道，是以無窮究精察之實。而周子之書不盡言，圖不盡意，蓋脉絡分明，而規模宏遠矣。是其優劣固不待辨，而謂其言之大畧相當者，不已過乎？執事猶以爲所優者乃在於人，而不在於言。夫即其言而考其行，韓子之爲人也，其平居則不過酣飲博奕之樂，其自負則止惟功名進取之念。其排佛老之功未有，而於潮州之竄寞，乃遂變。其處禍福死生之際，若《謝潮州表》及張籍侑奠之詞，則有愧於異學之流甚多。是其見道不精，而徒用力於言語文字之間者矣。

周子聞道甚早，信古好義，胷次洒落，而光風霽月之趣可挹；遇事剛果，而玉色金聲之著尤毅。其家甚約，而其意甚適；其取名甚短，而希世徼福之念甚薄。蓋其析之有以極其精而不亂，合之有
translation_en:
…contrary to the classics. His account of the spiritual power that wondrously animates the myriad things proceeds without becoming confined to either being or nonbeing. How could Yu understand this? Yu possessed very great natural gifts, but he apprehended the Way through literary composition; thus he lacked the actual work of exhaustive investigation and precise scrutiny. Master Zhou’s writings do not exhaust what he had to say, nor does his diagram exhaust his meaning; their underlying connections are clear, and their scope is broad and far-reaching. Their relative merits surely require no further discrimination. Is it not mistaken, then, to say that their statements are broadly equivalent? You, sir, nevertheless maintain that the superiority lies in the person rather than in his words. Now, if we examine their conduct in light of their words, Master Han—Han Yu—in his everyday life enjoyed nothing beyond heavy drinking and games of skill and chance; his ambitions extended only to achievement, reputation, and advancement. He had accomplished nothing in his rejection of Buddhism and Daoism before, upon his banishment to Chaozhou [?], he changed his position. In his conduct when confronted with misfortune and good fortune, life and death—as seen in the Memorial of Thanks from Chaozhou and the words of Zhang Ji’s sacrificial tribute—he had much to be ashamed of even in comparison with followers of heterodox teachings. His understanding of the Way was imprecise, and he merely exerted himself in speech and writing.

Master Zhou heard the Way very early, trusted antiquity, and loved righteousness. His heart was open and unencumbered, and one could savor in him the charm of a clear breeze and a moon emerging after rain. In handling affairs he was firm and decisive, and the manifest qualities of his jade-like countenance and bronze-like resonance were especially resolute. His household was very poor, yet his mind was thoroughly at ease. His pursuit of reputation was very limited [?], and he had little inclination to court the world’s favor or seek good fortune. For in analyzing it, he could reach its utmost subtlety without confusion; in bringing it together, he had…

title: 正德八年河南鄉試錄
text:
以盡其大而無餘則夫推明究極之精而
有以盡其藴者固其所也夫以其人大致
又相遠如此然則學者之所從違復何待
於他考而後爲凖哉雖然韓子特不及周
子爾秦漢而下至於隋唐異端之說盛行
而正學蕪矣愈獨推尊孟氏發明王道而
自託於不得其傳之後使天下復知有正
學者誰之力也嗚呼愈豈可少也哉謹對
第四問
吴瀚
===
同考試官教諭楊　批〔場中答此策者往往掇拾源流至論之緒餘而敷衍成篇殊無可人意者此荅有考據有折衷而〕
〔詞簡理明蓋不可以科舉文字視之也〕
同考試官學正鄧　批〔此策不難於荅而難於斷〕
〔制觀子之荅有斷制必有用之才矣〕
考試官學正王　批〔議論平正詞氣雍容比於騁浮〕
〔華以倖一得者遠矣〕
考試官教授陸　批〔典實之作參之前二場皆稱故〕
punctuated:
以盡其大而無餘，則夫推明究極之精而有以盡其藴者，固其所也。夫以其人大致又相遠如此，然則學者之所從違，復何待於他考而後爲凖哉？雖然，韓子特不及周子爾。秦漢而下，至於隋唐，異端之說盛行，而正學蕪矣。愈獨推尊孟氏，發明王道，而自託於不得其傳之後。使天下復知有正學者，誰之力也？嗚呼！愈豈可少也哉？謹對。

第四問
吴瀚

同考試官教諭楊　批〔場中答此策者，往往掇拾《源流至論》之緒餘而敷衍成篇，殊無可人意者。此荅有考據，有折衷，而〕〔詞簡理明，蓋不可以科舉文字視之也。〕

同考試官學正鄧　批〔此策不難於荅，而難於斷〕〔制。觀子之荅，有斷制，必有用之才矣。〕

考試官學正王　批〔議論平正，詞氣雍容，比於騁浮〕〔華以倖一得者，遠矣。〕

考試官教授陸　批〔典實之作，參之前二場，皆稱，故〕
translation_en:
…thereby encompassing its full greatness with nothing left over. Thus, elucidating its ultimate subtleties and fully bringing out its deeper meaning were naturally within his capacity. Since the two men differed so greatly in their general character, what further investigation must students await before establishing a standard for whom to follow and whom to reject? Nevertheless, Master Han fell short only of Master Zhou. From the Qin and Han down to the Sui and Tang, heterodox teachings flourished, while orthodox learning fell into neglect. Han Yu alone exalted Master Meng, elucidated the Way of the True King, and placed himself among those who came after its transmission had been lost. Through whose efforts did the world once again know that orthodox learning existed? Alas! Could Han Yu possibly be dispensed with? Respectfully submitted in reply.

Fourth Question
Wu Han

Comment by Associate Examiner Yang, Instructor: 〔Those answering this policy question in the examination hall often picked up scraps from Comprehensive Discussions of Origins and Developments (Yuanliu zhilun) and padded them out into essays; scarcely any were satisfactory. This answer offers substantiation from sources and balanced judgments, and〕〔its language is concise and its reasoning clear. It certainly should not be regarded merely as examination writing.〕

Comment by Associate Examiner Deng, School Director: 〔The difficulty of this policy question lies not in answering it but in reaching〕〔a firm judgment. Your answer shows such judgment; you surely possess talent that will prove useful.〕

Comment by Examiner Wang, School Director: 〔The arguments are balanced and sound, and the language and tone are poised and measured. It far surpasses those who flaunt empty〕〔ornament in hopes of a lucky success.〕

Comment by Examiner Lu, Professor: 〔A work grounded in authoritative sources and solid substance. Compared with the work from the preceding two sessions, all are of a comparable standard; therefore…〕

title: 正德八年河南鄉試錄
text:
取之
養士於學校則行業專而無他岐之惑取
士於貢舉則趨向正而絕倖進之途此實
求賢之要術圖治之良規也是以治天下
者必以此為當務之急焉甚矣賢才之有
益於人國然則當何如其作興長育而後
得其用邪古昔盛時陶和毓粹人之所以
自負者甚厚而其所以自進者甚重有不
待於學校之所養貢舉之所取也三代以
===
來上有以求于其下下有所待于其上然
黨庠遂序之法行鄉舉里選之法立而成
周致治亦由於是我
朝倣古為治用人之效其盛矣乎愚生有志
用世久矣而無由自達茲因執事所問試
一言之周室之季諸侯之士歲不以獻故
子產有不毀鄉校之議而學校之教無傳
焉嬴秦之後智謀之士各逞其雄故漢高
有不事詩書之失而學校之教無聞焉觀
punctuated:
取之。

養士於學校，則行業專而無他岐之惑；取士於貢舉，則趨向正而絕倖進之途。此實求賢之要術、圖治之良規也。是以治天下者，必以此為當務之急焉。甚矣，賢才之有益於人國！然則當何如其作興長育，而後得其用邪？古昔盛時，陶和毓粹，人之所以自負者甚厚，而其所以自進者甚重，有不待於學校之所養、貢舉之所取也。三代以來，上有以求于其下，下有所待于其上。然黨庠遂序之法行，鄉舉里選之法立，而成周致治亦由於是。我朝倣古為治，用人之效，其盛矣乎！愚生有志用世久矣，而無由自達。茲因執事所問，試一言之。周室之季，諸侯之士歲不以獻，故子產有不毀鄉校之議，而學校之教無傳焉。嬴秦之後，智謀之士各逞其雄，故漢高有不事詩書之失，而學校之教無聞焉。觀
translation_en:
…he was therefore selected.

When scholars are nurtured in schools, their conduct and studies remain focused, without the confusion of divergent paths; when scholars are selected through tribute examinations, their aspirations are properly directed, and the road to advancement by mere good fortune is closed. These are indeed essential methods for seeking worthy men and sound principles for pursuing good government. Thus those who govern All under Heaven must regard them as urgent priorities. How greatly worthy and talented men benefit a state! How, then, should they be encouraged and nurtured so that their abilities may be put to use?

In the flourishing ages of antiquity, harmony was cultivated and purity nurtured. People had substantial grounds for confidence in themselves and treated their own advancement with great seriousness; they did not necessarily depend upon nurture in schools or selection through tribute examinations. From the Three Dynasties onward, those above had means of seeking talent among those below, while those below looked to those above. The system of district and suburban schools was implemented, and the system of recommendation from townships and selection from villages was established. The achievement of good government under the Zhou likewise arose from these arrangements. Our dynasty models its government on antiquity: how splendid have been the results of its employment of men!

This humble student has long aspired to serve the world, but has had no means of making himself known. Now, prompted by your question, I venture to offer a few words. In the closing years of the Zhou royal house, the regional lords no longer presented their scholars annually. Thus, although Zichan argued against destroying the township schools, school instruction was not handed down. After the Qin of the Ying house, men of intelligence and strategy each sought to display their prowess. Thus Gaozu of Han erred in neglecting the Odes and the Documents, and school instruction was unheard of. Considering…

title: 正德八年河南鄉試錄
text:
此則凡後世養士之不備槩可見也唐之
取士既有學館生徒州縣鄉貢矣又復別
立制舉而不專於鄉校宋之取士既有賢
良之舉進士之科矣又復增以漕試而兼
考其行藝觀此則凡後世取士之未盡亦
可知也是以徇名責實之意廢敦本務實
之風微而成周良法更變已不知其幾也
祖宗設學校以教天下之士亦因成周黨庠遂
序之法而爲之爾日省之月試之而歲一
===
考之蓋以學校者教化之本源舍是將無
以責其成矣設貢舉以取天下之士亦因
成周鄉舉里選之法而行之爾舉于鄉貢
于禮部而策于
大廷蓋以貢舉者取人之正途舍是將無以招
其至矣是則法之盡善固無容議其所可
言者特以學校之養固欲得人以資用也
然吏出送入而習爲浮華進寸退尺而倖
於聲利行業已不專矣尚何望焉貢舉之
punctuated:
此則凡後世養士之不備，槩可見也。唐之取士，既有學館生徒、州縣鄉貢矣，又復別立制舉，而不專於鄉校。宋之取士，既有賢良之舉、進士之科矣，又復增以漕試，而兼考其行藝。觀此，則凡後世取士之未盡，亦可知也。是以徇名責實之意廢，敦本務實之風微，而成周良法更變已不知其幾也。
祖宗設學校以教天下之士，亦因成周黨庠遂序之法而爲之爾。日省之，月試之，而歲一考之，蓋以學校者教化之本源，舍是將無以責其成矣。設貢舉以取天下之士，亦因成周鄉舉里選之法而行之爾。舉于鄉，貢于禮部，而策于大廷，蓋以貢舉者取人之正途，舍是將無以招其至矣。是則法之盡善，固無容議。其所可言者，特以學校之養，固欲得人以資用也，然吏出送入，而習爲浮華，進寸退尺，而倖於聲利，行業已不專矣，尚何望焉？貢舉之
translation_en:
…from this, the inadequacies of later ages in nurturing scholars can generally be seen. In selecting scholars, the Tang already drew upon students of educational institutions and candidates recommended by prefectures and counties; yet it also separately established special examinations by imperial decree, rather than relying exclusively on local schools. In selecting scholars, the Song already had recommendations of the worthy and good and the metropolitan graduate (jinshi) examination category; yet it further added examinations conducted by the transport commissions, assessing candidates’ conduct as well as their literary attainments. From this, the shortcomings of later ages in selecting scholars can also be understood. Thus the intention of following reputation while demanding actual merit was abandoned, and the practice of strengthening fundamentals and pursuing substance declined. The fine institutions of the Zhou at its flourishing height underwent countless changes.
Our imperial ancestors established schools to instruct scholars throughout the realm, simply following the Zhou system of schools in the dang and sui administrative units. Students were inspected daily, tested monthly, and examined once each year, for schools are the fountainhead of moral instruction: without them, there would be no means of holding students accountable for their achievement. They established the system of recommendation and examination to select scholars throughout the realm, likewise following the Zhou practice of recommending men through townships and selecting them through village communities. Candidates were recommended at the provincial level, presented to the Ministry of Rites, and examined on policy at the imperial court. For recommendation and examination constitute the proper path for recruiting men; without this, there would be no means of drawing them into service. The complete excellence of these institutions is therefore beyond dispute. What may be discussed is only this: schools nurture scholars precisely to obtain men fit for employment. Yet amid officials’ departures and ceremonial receptions [?], scholars become accustomed to superficial display; they advance an inch and retreat a foot, seeking reputation and profit through good fortune. Their conduct and studies are already lacking in single-minded dedication. What further hope can there be? As for the system of recommendation and examination…

title: 正德八年河南鄉試錄
text:
科固欲求賢以圖治也乎□紈子弟得預
計偕驕惰鄙夫濫登仕籍趨向已不正矣
餘何望焉爲今之計必擇剛毅方正之人
以居師儒之職則所養之士必端矣何至
士風之不振乎擇忠厚正直之人以居考
校之任則取士必得矣何至士習之大壞
乎雖然成天下之治者在機不在勢運天
下之機者在上不在下方今
聖天子操制作之機而賢公卿大夫又相與協
===
力于下所養所取莫非正人其所以治隆
俗美寔有望于
今日愚生菲薄而言之及此出位之罪也執事
以爲何如
第五問
同考試官教諭林　批
尹倫
時務策荅者多試問目逐
何敷衍而此作獨不然他人之所詳者我畧他人之所畧者我詳
可不謂有識之士乎
punctuated:
科，固欲求賢以圖治也。乎□紈子弟得預計偕，驕惰鄙夫濫登仕籍，趨向已不正矣，餘何望焉？爲今之計，必擇剛毅方正之人以居師儒之職，則所養之士必端矣，何至士風之不振乎？擇忠厚正直之人以居考校之任，則取士必得矣，何至士習之大壞乎？雖然，成天下之治者在機不在勢，運天下之機者在上不在下。方今聖天子操制作之機，而賢公卿大夫又相與協力于下，所養所取莫非正人，其所以治隆俗美，寔有望于今日。愚生菲薄，而言之及此，出位之罪也。執事以爲何如？
第五問
同考試官教諭林　批
尹倫
時務策荅者，多試問目逐何敷衍，而此作獨不然。他人之所詳者我畧，他人之所畧者我詳，可不謂有識之士乎？
translation_en:
…The examination system is surely intended to seek worthy men in order to achieve good government. Yet [?] sons of wealthy families in silken clothes are allowed to join the candidates proceeding to the capital, and arrogant, indolent, vulgar men indiscriminately enter the ranks of officeholders. Their aspirations are already misguided: what further hope can there be? The plan for the present must be to select resolute and upright men to hold teaching posts. The scholars they nurture will then assuredly be upright; how could scholarly morale fail to flourish? Select men of loyalty, generosity, and integrity to undertake examining duties, and the selection of scholars will assuredly yield suitable men. How could scholars’ conduct deteriorate so greatly?
Nevertheless, bringing good government to the realm depends on the pivotal means of action, not on the weight of circumstances; directing those means rests with those above, not those below. Now the sagely Son of Heaven commands the means of establishing institutions, while worthy dukes, ministers, and grandees cooperate in support below. Those nurtured and selected will all be upright men. There is indeed hope today for flourishing government and fine customs. I, an unworthy student of meager abilities, have ventured to speak thus far and am guilty of speaking beyond my station. What does Your Excellency think?
Fifth Question
Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor
Yin Lun
Those answering policy questions on current affairs mostly elaborate upon the question’s wording item by item [?], but this composition alone does otherwise. What others treat at length, I treat briefly; what others treat briefly, I treat at length. Can he not be called a scholar of discernment?

title: 正德八年河南鄉試錄
text:
考試官學正王　批〔策問中有許多說話而此荅能畧之豈謂事已往者自不必致論邪〕
考試官教授陸　批〔不爲問目所窘眞策手也〕
論天下之事不可不先事而憂任天下之
事不可不先事而處論事而不知所憂必
不能得事之情任事而不知所處必不能
勝事之責不能得事之情則不足與論事
不能勝事之責則不可使任事天下之事
多矣今之論事者有能盡知所憂者乎今
===
之任事者有能盡知所處者乎而執事以
兵與食下詢承學謂時務之急非一而此
尤今日之所當議者執事寔寄憂於此不
知執事之所欲先事而處者何如諸生不
敢爲出位之思雖然亦嘗於此憂焉既承
明問敢無詞以復乎請自兵言之古者寓
兵於民三時務農一時講武六鄉之内六
軍屬焉六遂之内軍又倍焉卒有四方之
役畿内之兵不出而二伯專征諸侯共之
punctuated:
考試官學正王批〔策問中有許多說話，而此荅能畧之，豈謂事已往者自不必致論邪？〕

考試官教授陸批〔不爲問目所窘，眞策手也。〕

論天下之事，不可不先事而憂；任天下之事，不可不先事而處。論事而不知所憂，必不能得事之情；任事而不知所處，必不能勝事之責。不能得事之情，則不足與論事；不能勝事之責，則不可使任事。天下之事多矣，今之論事者，有能盡知所憂者乎？今之任事者，有能盡知所處者乎？而執事以兵與食下詢承學，謂時務之急非一，而此尤今日之所當議者。執事寔寄憂於此，不知執事之所欲先事而處者何如？諸生不敢爲出位之思，雖然，亦嘗於此憂焉。既承明問，敢無詞以復乎？請自兵言之。古者寓兵於民，三時務農，一時講武。六鄉之内，六軍屬焉；六遂之内，軍又倍焉。卒有四方之役，畿内之兵不出，而二伯專征，諸侯共之。
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Wang, School Instructor: 〔The policy question contains many points, yet this answer manages to pass over them briefly. Does the writer mean that matters already past need not be discussed?〕

Comment by Examiner Lu, Professor: 〔Unconstrained by the question’s individual points—a true master of the policy essay.〕

Those who discuss the affairs of the realm must anticipate causes for concern; those who take responsibility for the affairs of the realm must make provision before events arise. To discuss affairs without knowing what warrants concern is necessarily to fail to grasp their true circumstances. To take responsibility for affairs without knowing how to handle them is necessarily to be unequal to that responsibility. Those who cannot grasp the true circumstances of affairs are unfit to join in discussing them; those unequal to the responsibility for affairs cannot be entrusted with their management. The affairs of the realm are many. Among those who discuss them today, is there anyone who fully understands what warrants concern? Among those who take responsibility for them today, is there anyone who fully understands what measures to take?

You, sir, have condescended to question us students about troops and food supplies, saying that although the urgent concerns of the day are numerous, these especially call for discussion today. Your concern indeed rests upon these matters. I wonder what measures you would wish to take in anticipation of events. We students dare not entertain thoughts beyond our station; nevertheless, these matters have also caused us concern. Having received your discerning question, dare I offer no words in reply?

Let me begin with troops. In antiquity, soldiers were incorporated within the common people: for three seasons they devoted themselves to farming, and for one season they practiced military skills. Within the six inner districts were organized six armies; within the six outer districts, the armies were twice that number. If a campaign suddenly arose in any quarter, the troops within the royal domain did not march out. Instead, the two regional overlords exercised authority over punitive expeditions, and the feudal lords supplied the forces.

title: 正德八年河南鄉試錄
text:
其或家宰徵師不過元戎十乘爲啓行之
先耳而調兵諸侯各從其方之便不聞有
奔命之勞也諸侯□□□王命不敢私用
其用之也所在皆庠序隊射御之士其
不用也所在皆力農桑知孝弟之民不聞
其征調之苦也請自食言之古者京畿千
里自甸服百里賦納總至於五百里米而
五百之外皆諸侯國不過任土作貢以輸
王府而賦稅米粟則未嘗徵之當時宗廟
===
百官有司之事軍旅之需千里之內賦稅
取之而自足不聞其仰餉運於畿外之諸
侯糴米粟於畿內之百姓也三年耕而餘
一年之積九年作而有三年之儲雖水旱
爲災不聞其有捐瘠之民也後世井田廢
而兵民分封建罷而郡縣置舉天下之丁
夫惟上之役盡天下之賦稅惟上之供□
兵之與食視三代顧有不足之憂是必有
其故也兵之不足政失之也食之不足事
punctuated:
其或家宰徵師，不過元戎十乘，爲啓行之先耳。而調兵，諸侯各從其方之便，不聞有奔命之勞也。諸侯□□□王命，不敢私用。其用之也，所在皆庠序隊射御之士；其不用也，所在皆力農桑、知孝弟之民，不聞其征調之苦也。
請自食言之。古者京畿千里，自甸服百里賦納總，至於五百里米，而五百之外皆諸侯國，不過任土作貢，以輸王府，而賦稅米粟則未嘗徵之。當時宗廟、百官有司之事，軍旅之需，千里之內賦稅取之而自足，不聞其仰餉運於畿外之諸侯，糴米粟於畿內之百姓也。三年耕而餘一年之積，九年作而有三年之儲，雖水旱爲災，不聞其有捐瘠之民也。
後世井田廢而兵民分，封建罷而郡縣置，舉天下之丁夫，惟上之役；盡天下之賦稅，惟上之供。□兵之與食，視三代顧有不足之憂，是必有其故也。兵之不足，政失之也；食之不足，事
translation_en:
…If the Grand Steward occasionally levied troops, these amounted to no more than ten great war chariots serving as the vanguard to open the way. When troops were mobilized, each regional lord acted as local circumstances allowed; one hears of no exhausting rush to obey commands. The regional lords [three illegible characters] the king’s command [?] and dared not deploy troops for private purposes. When employed, the men everywhere were men of the local schools trained in archery and charioteering [?]; when not employed, they were people who labored at farming and sericulture and understood filial piety and respect for elder brothers. One hears of no suffering caused by their conscription and mobilization.
Let me now speak of food supplies. In antiquity, the capital domain extended a thousand li. Within the royal domain, tax deliveries ranged from whole grain stalks in the innermost hundred li to husked grain at five hundred li. Beyond five hundred li lay the states of the regional lords, which merely sent tribute to the royal treasury according to their lands’ products; grain taxes were never levied upon them. At that time, the requirements of the ancestral temples, the various officials and responsible offices, and the armies were adequately met by taxes collected within the thousand-li domain. One hears of no dependence on provisions transported from regional lords outside the capital domain, or purchases of grain from commoners within it. Three years of cultivation left a surplus sufficient for one year, and nine years of work produced reserves sufficient for three years. Even when floods or droughts brought disaster, one hears of no people abandoned to starvation [?].
In later ages, the well-field system was abolished, and soldiers and civilians became separate. The system of enfeoffment was ended, and prefectures and counties were established. All the able-bodied men under Heaven were subject to service for the ruler; all the taxes under Heaven supplied his needs. [One illegible character] Yet, compared with the Three Dynasties, there was anxiety over shortages of troops and food. This must have had its causes. The shortage of troops resulted from failures in governance; the shortage of food, from undertakings …

title: 正德八年河南鄉試錄
text:
耗之也三代無論姑舉漢事以明今日之
始末漢初南軍守宮北軍護京師調發郡
國材官騎士分番為之又選天下材力武
猛者以為輕車騎士材官樓船各於其地
所宜講課武事平地用車騎山阻用材官
水泉用樓船制為近古及光武之世都試
既罷外兵不練雖疆埸之間復因外寇增
廣屯戍而國有征伐終藉京師之軍以出
自建元以及漢衰連年暴露荼旅無復鎮
===
衛之職此政之失也今之兵制能守
祖宗之法而無變焉一如漢高祖時列郡有守
有都尉都尉佐太守典武職甲卒王國則
以内史比郡守中尉比都尉侯國則亦有
相秩比令長每歲八月會太守郡尉令長
相丞咸預各以其方之所習而課殿最焉
强幹弱枝防微杜漸體統周密倖有盜賊
何假於
禁兵邊兵又土軍之調發臨時而取辦乎漢
punctuated:
耗之也。三代無論，姑舉漢事，以明今日之始末。漢初，南軍守宮，北軍護京師，調發郡國材官、騎士，分番為之。又選天下材力武猛者，以為輕車、騎士、材官、樓船，各於其地所宜，講課武事。平地用車騎，山阻用材官，水泉用樓船，制為近古。及光武之世，都試既罷，外兵不練，雖疆埸之間復因外寇增廣屯戍，而國有征伐，終藉京師之軍以出。自建元以及漢衰，連年暴露荼旅，無復鎮衛之職，此政之失也。
今之兵制能守祖宗之法而無變焉，一如漢高祖時，列郡有守、有都尉，都尉佐太守典武職甲卒；王國則以内史比郡守，中尉比都尉；侯國則亦有相，秩比令長。每歲八月會，太守、郡尉、令長、相、丞咸預，各以其方之所習而課殿最焉。强幹弱枝，防微杜漸，體統周密，倖有盜賊，何假於禁兵、邊兵，又土軍之調發，臨時而取辦乎？漢
translation_en:
…is because undertakings consume it. Leaving aside the Three Dynasties, let us take events of the Han to illuminate how the present situation arose. In the early Han, the Southern Army guarded the palace, and the Northern Army protected the capital. Selected infantry and cavalry were levied from the commanderies and kingdoms to serve in rotation. Men of physical strength and martial prowess were also selected throughout the empire to serve in light chariot units, cavalry, selected infantry, and tower-ship forces. Military training and assessment were conducted according to the conditions appropriate to each locality. Chariots and cavalry were used on level ground, selected infantry in rugged mountains, and tower ships on waterways. This system closely resembled that of antiquity. By the reign of Guangwu, however, the general military reviews had been abolished, and troops outside the capital went untrained. Although frontier garrisons were again expanded in response to foreign incursions, whenever the state undertook a campaign it ultimately relied on troops dispatched from the capital. From the Jianyuan era [?] down to the decline of the Han, these troops endured years of exposure and hardship on campaign [?], no longer performing their duties of garrisoning and guarding. This was a failure of governance.
If the military system of today could preserve the laws of our imperial ancestors without alteration, it would be just as in the time of Gaozu of Han. Each commandery had an Administrator and a Commandant; the Commandant assisted the Administrator in overseeing military offices and armed troops. In the kingdoms, the Chamberlain for the Capital corresponded to the commandery Administrator, and the Capital Commandant to the commandery Commandant. The marquisates likewise had Chancellors, whose ranks corresponded to those of county Magistrates and Chiefs. Assemblies were held in the eighth month of each year, attended by the Administrators, commandery Commandants, county Magistrates and Chiefs, Chancellors, and Assistant Magistrates. Each contingent was assessed and ranked according to the skills practiced in its locality. This strengthened the trunk and weakened the branches, guarding against trouble at its slightest beginnings and preventing its gradual growth; the organizational structure was comprehensive and closely knit. Should bandits happen to appear, what need would there be to dispatch palace troops, frontier troops, or local troops, hastily arranging matters when the occasion arose? Under the Han…

title: 正德八年河南鄉試錄
text:
文帝時封國漸衆諸侯王自食其地王府
所入蓋寡又與匈奴和親歲致金繒後數
爲邊患天子親將出擊復因河決有築塞
勞費大司農財用宜不致充溢而文帝在
位十二年即賜民田租次年遂除之粟陳
貫朽以貽武帝之世乃外事四夷内興土
功用度不足遂募民入奴婢得以終身復
及入羊爲郎又令民買爵置武功爵造皮
幣白金置鹽鐵均輸官筭商車緡錢榷酒
===
酤卒之盜賊蠭起而有輪臺之悔此事之
耗也今之賦稅能守
祖宗之法而無變焉一如漢文帝時恭儉在上
百金之費亦不苟用宮闈是儆流傳國都
莫有奢侈之習海内富庶家給人足天下
之治清和咸理自無他變萬一不虞何暇
於
内帑邊儲之借與輸納銀粟之令當事而會
計乎若夫執事所謂壯丁之增今無事之
punctuated:
文帝時，封國漸衆，諸侯王自食其地，王府所入蓋寡。又與匈奴和親，歲致金繒，後數爲邊患，天子親將出擊。復因河決，有築塞勞費，大司農財用宜不致充溢。而文帝在位十二年，即賜民田租，次年遂除之。粟陳貫朽，以貽武帝之世，乃外事四夷，内興土功，用度不足，遂募民入奴婢，得以終身復，及入羊爲郎。又令民買爵，置武功爵，造皮幣、白金，置鹽鐵、均輸官，筭商車緡錢，榷酒酤。卒之盜賊蠭起，而有輪臺之悔，此事之耗也。
今之賦稅，能守祖宗之法而無變焉，一如漢文帝時，恭儉在上，百金之費亦不苟用，宮闈是儆，流傳國都，莫有奢侈之習，海内富庶，家給人足，天下之治，清和咸理，自無他變。萬一不虞，何暇於内帑、邊儲之借與輸納銀粟之令，當事而會計乎？若夫執事所謂壯丁之增，今無事之
translation_en:
… in Emperor Wen’s reign, the number of enfeoffed kingdoms gradually increased. The princes drew their revenues directly from their own territories, so receipts into the royal treasury [?] were presumably small. Moreover, marriage alliances were concluded with the Xiongnu, with annual gifts of gold and silk; subsequently, they repeatedly caused trouble on the frontier, and the emperor personally led troops against them. Breaches of the Yellow River also entailed labor and expense in building embankments and closing the breaches. The funds available to the Chamberlain for the National Treasury could hardly have been abundant. Yet in the twelfth year of his reign, Emperor Wen remitted the people’s land tax, and the following year abolished it altogether. Grain grew old in the granaries, and the strings of stored coins rotted away: such was the legacy passed down to Emperor Wu’s age. Then campaigns were undertaken against the peoples beyond the borders, while construction projects were launched at home. When funds proved insufficient, people were invited to surrender male and female slaves in exchange for lifelong exemption from service, and to contribute sheep [?] in exchange for appointment as gentlemen of the palace. People were also permitted to purchase ranks of nobility; military-merit ranks were established; leather currency and white-metal coins were produced; officials were appointed to administer salt, iron, and equitable transport; taxes were levied on merchants’ carts and strings of cash; and a monopoly was imposed on the sale of liquor. In the end, bandits rose in swarms, and there came the repentance expressed at Luntai. Such was the drain caused by these undertakings.
If taxation today could adhere without alteration to the laws of our imperial ancestors, following precisely the example of Emperor Wen of Han, with reverence and frugality practiced at the top, even an expenditure of a hundred units of gold would not be made lightly. The palace women would take heed, and this example would spread throughout the capital, leaving no habits of extravagance. All within the seas would be prosperous, every household adequately supplied and every person provided for. The realm would be peacefully and harmoniously governed, with everything in order, and naturally there would be no further disturbances. But should an unforeseen emergency occur, what time would there be, once confronted with it, to calculate borrowings from the palace treasury and frontier reserves, or to issue orders for contributions of silver and grain? As for the increase in able-bodied men that you, sir, have mentioned, now, in a time free from trouble …

title: 正德八年河南鄉試錄
text:
時籍其人而團結敎集必將廢其生理而
又使之自備器械自齎食用必有所不能
辦將以食于官則官亦不給將以免其正
差則均徭之在所司紛如牛毛又將移之
誰乎吏姦黠者與之爲市家至戶到追胥
迫脅錄放之間害民滋益多而事終無所
濟若彼民壯令甲所著當免羨丁以貼助
其役今有司審編中間丁單力弱無所仰
給不能自脫者亦多矣終歲奔走豈專爲
===
城守計貪冒之徒又從而科削之爲今之
計州縣獨可照額選補民壯精健勇敢務
足其數倣宋弓箭社槍仗手管操官員以
時敎習驗覆等第致其賞罰凡例所應優
免有糧免糧有丁免丁以惠恤之大州縣
蓋數百人小縣亦百十餘人緩急遣用豈
不亦可助戎行之不足邪也地之淸河南
民俗方健此訟始因年儉棄賣祖業漂流
異鄉經涉數代歸還廬井鄰里非舊桑榆
punctuated:
時，籍其人而團結敎集，必將廢其生理，而又使之自備器械、自齎食用，必有所不能辦。將以食于官，則官亦不給；將以免其正差，則均徭之在所司紛如牛毛，又將移之誰乎？吏姦黠者與之爲市，家至戶到，追胥迫脅，錄放之間，害民滋益多，而事終無所濟。若彼民壯，令甲所著，當免羨丁以貼助其役。今有司審編，中間丁單力弱、無所仰給、不能自脫者亦多矣。終歲奔走，豈專爲城守計？貪冒之徒又從而科削之。爲今之計，州縣獨可照額選補民壯，精健勇敢，務足其數。倣宋弓箭社、槍仗手，管操官員以時敎習，驗覆等第，致其賞罰。凡例所應優免，有糧免糧，有丁免丁，以惠恤之。大州縣蓋數百人，小縣亦百十餘人，緩急遣用，豈不亦可助戎行之不足邪？
也地之淸河南，民俗方健。此訟始因年儉，棄賣祖業，漂流異鄉，經涉數代，歸還廬井，鄰里非舊，桑榆
translation_en:
…in such times, registering these men, organizing them into units, and assembling them for training will surely disrupt their livelihoods. If they must also supply their own weapons and equipment and bring their own provisions, there will certainly be requirements they cannot meet. If the government is to feed them, it too lacks sufficient supplies. If they are to be exempted from their regular service obligations, the equitable corvée assignments administered by the responsible offices are already as numerous and tangled as ox hairs: to whom will these obligations then be transferred? Crafty clerks will turn the process into a business, going from house to house, pursuing and coercing people. In deciding whom to enroll and whom to release, they will inflict ever greater harm upon the people, while ultimately accomplishing nothing.
As for the local militiamen, the statutes stipulate that surplus able-bodied males should be exempted from service so that they can help support the militiamen’s duties. Yet among those whom the authorities now examine and enroll, many belong to households with only one able-bodied man and scant resources, have no means of support, and cannot extricate themselves. They spend the entire year running on errands: can this really be solely for the defense of the city? Greedy and unscrupulous men then impose further levies and exactions upon them.
The appropriate course now is simply for prefectures and counties to select and replenish their local militia according to the established quotas, choosing fit, vigorous, and courageous men and ensuring that the required numbers are filled. Following the example of the Song archery societies and spearmen, officers responsible for drill should train them at regular intervals, examine and reassess their grades, and administer rewards and punishments accordingly. All preferential exemptions prescribed by regulation should be granted: exempt grain obligations where there are grain obligations, and manpower obligations where there are manpower obligations, thus providing relief and support. Large prefectures and counties would have several hundred men, and even small counties a hundred or somewhat more. If dispatched when needed, could they not help make up deficiencies in the military ranks?
Concerning the land in Qing, Henan [?], the local people are upright and vigorous. This litigation originated when poor harvests forced people to abandon or sell their ancestral properties and wander in other regions. After several generations, they returned to their former homes, but their neighbors were no longer the same, and the mulberry and elm trees…

title: 正德八年河南鄉試錄
text:
段植年載既久易生假冒遠認死亡之族
旁引親舊之人或許水退地出或稱產去
稅存孰官孰私莫可取據良疇委而不開
桑枯而不採寔由經界未正故也愚以
爲所爭之地宜限年斷事久難明悉屬今
主亦息訟之一端若夫補稅額之舊逋蓋
不係此今谷州縣民戶有有稅無田者有
有田無稅者或緣侵耕失稅或推割不行
或兵火後稅籍不存彼此求脫或詭名寄
===
產或逃戶遺稅逃田積稅人得推託負責
奉里藏情隱姦致爭非一有司能就本里
以無田之稅均增於原額之田無稅之田
減均於原額之稅人已稱善不知減均得
偏輕之利而均增得偏重之害也爲今之
計宜依朱子漳州經界奏札推擇官吏委
任責成步算畝數攢造圖帳貫從官出隨
產均稅特許過鄉通戶均紐廣幾百里之
內輕重齊同一邑行之既恊人情移之他
punctuated: 段植，年載既久，易生假冒，遠認死亡之族，旁引親舊之人，或許水退地出，或稱產去稅存，孰官孰私，莫可取據。良疇委而不開，桑枯而不採，寔由經界未正故也。愚以爲所爭之地，宜限年斷事，久難明，悉屬今主，亦息訟之一端。若夫補稅額之舊逋，蓋不係此。今谷州縣民戶，有有稅無田者，有有田無稅者，或緣侵耕失稅，或推割不行，或兵火後稅籍不存，彼此求脫，或詭名寄產，或逃戶遺稅、逃田積稅，人得推託，負責奉里，藏情隱姦，致爭非一。有司能就本里，以無田之稅均增於原額之田，無稅之田減均於原額之稅，人已稱善，不知減均得偏輕之利，而均增得偏重之害也。爲今之計，宜依朱子《漳州經界奏札》，推擇官吏，委任責成，步算畝數，攢造圖帳，貫從官出，隨產均稅，特許過鄉通戶均紐，廣幾百里之內，輕重齊同。一邑行之，既恊人情，移之他
translation_en:
…the plantings [?]. With so many years having passed, fraudulent claims readily arise: people claim distant kinship with deceased families or invoke collateral connections with relatives and old acquaintances. Some claim that land emerged when the waters receded; others say that the property is gone but its tax liability remains. There is no reliable evidence for determining what belongs to the government and what is privately owned. Good fields lie abandoned and untilled; mulberry trees wither without their leaves being gathered. This is indeed because land boundaries have not been properly established. In my humble opinion, disputes over land should be adjudicated with a limit on how far back claims may reach. Where a case is too old to clarify, the land should belong entirely to its present holder. This, too, would be one means of ending litigation. Making up old arrears in the assessed taxes, however, is a separate matter.

Among households in the prefectures and counties today [?], some owe taxes but have no land, while others have land but owe no taxes. This may result from encroachment and cultivation without payment of taxes, or from failure to transfer and apportion tax liabilities when land changes hands. Sometimes tax registers were lost during warfare, and each party seeks to escape liability. Others lodge property under false names, or absconding households leave unpaid taxes and abandoned fields accumulate arrears. People thus find grounds for evading responsibility, leaving the burden upon the village [?]. Concealed circumstances and hidden fraud give rise to disputes of many kinds. If the responsible officials can redistribute, within the same village, taxes without corresponding land as an added levy on land already assessed, and use untaxed land to reduce and redistribute the existing tax assessment, people already praise this as good administration. They do not realize that the reduced assessment gives some the advantage of an unduly light burden, while the added levy subjects others to an unduly heavy one.

The appropriate plan now is to follow Master Zhu’s Memorial on the Land Survey in Zhangzhou: select officials and clerks, entrust them with the task, and hold them responsible for completing it; measure and calculate the acreage in mu, and compile maps and registers, with the documentation issued by the authorities [?]. Taxes should be equitably assessed according to property holdings. Special permission should be given to equalize assessments across township boundaries and among households, so that throughout an area extending several hundred li, tax burdens are made uniform. Once this has been implemented in one county and has accorded with the people’s wishes, extend it to other…

title: 正德八年河南鄉試錄
text:
郡當無不可行者然行之詳則足爲一定
之法行之畧則適生他日之弊此責成之
要得人也執事之所憂而所欲處者豈止
是而已乎民壯田税在執事處之易易耳
兵食之大者廟堂之議必將以入告于吾
聖天子易傳有之節以制度不傷財不害民不
傷財則不害民矣不傷財則足食而不害
民則足兵矣宋人黄紙放白紙催行於赦
令之餘初刺手繼刺面見於赦榜之後然
則孔子所謂足兵民信之者獨何歟謹對
punctuated: 郡，當無不可行者。然行之詳，則足爲一定之法；行之畧，則適生他日之弊。此責成之要，得人也。執事之所憂而所欲處者，豈止是而已乎？民壯、田税，在執事處之易易耳。兵食之大者，廟堂之議必將以入告于吾聖天子。《易傳》有之：「節以制度，不傷財，不害民。」不傷財，則不害民矣；不傷財，則足食，而不害民，則足兵矣。宋人黄紙放、白紙催，行於赦令之餘；初刺手、繼刺面，見於赦榜之後。然則孔子所謂「足兵，民信之」者，獨何歟？謹對。
translation_en:
… commanderies, there should be none in which it cannot be implemented. Yet if implemented thoroughly, it can become a settled rule; if implemented cursorily, it will only give rise to abuses in days to come. The essential point in assigning responsibility for its accomplishment is to obtain the right people. Surely these are not the only matters that concern you and that you wish to address? Local militia and land taxes are easy enough for you to manage. As for the larger matters of military preparedness and food supplies, the court’s deliberations will surely be submitted to our sagely Son of Heaven.

The Commentary on the Changes says: “Regulate through institutions and measures, without damaging resources or harming the people.” If resources are not damaged, the people will not be harmed. Preserving resources ensures sufficient food; avoiding harm to the people ensures sufficient troops. Under the Song, “remission on yellow paper, demands for payment on white paper” occurred in the wake of amnesty decrees; “first tattooing the hands, then tattooing the face” occurred after the posting of amnesty proclamations. What, then, did Confucius mean by “sufficient troops” and “the people’s trust”? I respectfully submit this reply.

title: 正德八年河南鄉試錄
text:
河南鄉試錄後序
論學術於三代之後者必以
宋爲上漢次之唐爲下夫漢
唐所以不及宋者非其文不
足也特所務者文焉而已矣
有宋眞儒繼作而堯舜禹湯
文武周孔千載不傳之緒賴
以復明士生斯時幸矣然目
以朋黨斥以僞學乃使道學
之名爲世大禁而眞儒之用
不獲盡展此寔幸中之不幸
者我
祖宗創業垂統
聖子神孫嗣守鴻圖百五十年于
punctuated:
河南鄉試錄後序

論學術於三代之後者，必以宋爲上，漢次之，唐爲下。夫漢唐所以不及宋者，非其文不足也，特所務者文焉而已矣。有宋眞儒繼作，而堯舜禹湯文武周孔千載不傳之緒，賴以復明。士生斯時，幸矣！然目以朋黨，斥以僞學，乃使道學之名爲世大禁，而眞儒之用不獲盡展，此寔幸中之不幸者。我祖宗創業垂統，聖子神孫嗣守鴻圖，百五十年于
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Henan Provincial Examination

Those who discuss scholarship after the Three Dynasties invariably rank the Song highest, the Han next, and the Tang lowest. The reason the Han and Tang did not equal the Song was not that their literary accomplishments were insufficient, but that literature alone was their concern. Under the Song, true Confucian scholars arose in succession. Through them, the tradition of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Kings Wen and Wu, Zhou Gong, and Kongzi, whose transmission had lapsed for a thousand years, was brought to light again. How fortunate were scholars born in that age! Yet these scholars were branded as a faction and their learning denounced as false, so that even the name “Learning of the Way” became a great taboo of the age, and true Confucians could not fully put their abilities into practice. This was indeed misfortune amid good fortune.

Our imperial ancestors founded the dynasty and handed down its succession. Their sage sons and divine grandsons have inherited and preserved their grand undertaking for a hundred and fifty years …

title: 正德八年河南鄉試錄
text:
茲一惟敦尚名教尊崇正學
人非堯舜禹湯文武周孔之
書不讀學非堯舜禹湯文武
周孔之道不用以故士之所
業粹然歸於純正殆復過于
宋馬漢唐無論也正德癸酉
秋河南例當開科取士凡執
===
事者咸祗若
國家盛典矢心殫力莫敢怠遑
振作士類視昔有加而所取
士有限者遵
定制爾錄既成學夔濫竽考校
之末宜序諸末簡噫士不幸
生不逢時猶當違俗以強學
punctuated:
茲，一惟敦尚名教，尊崇正學。人非堯舜禹湯文武周孔之書不讀，學非堯舜禹湯文武周孔之道不用。以故士之所業，粹然歸於純正，殆復過于宋馬，漢唐無論也。
正德癸酉秋，河南例當開科取士。凡執事者，咸祗若國家盛典，矢心殫力，莫敢怠遑，振作士類，視昔有加。而所取士有限者，遵定制爾。
錄既成，學夔濫竽考校之末，宜序諸末簡。噫！士不幸生不逢時，猶當違俗以強學。
translation_en:
…down to the present, consistently esteeming moral teaching and honoring orthodox learning. Men read only the writings of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Kings Wen and Wu, the Duke of Zhou, and Confucius; in their learning they apply only the Way of these sages. Consequently, the studies pursued by scholars have become wholly pure and orthodox, perhaps even surpassing those of the Song [?], to say nothing of the Han and Tang.
In the autumn of the guiyou year of Zhengde [1513], Henan was due, according to established practice, to hold the examination and select scholars. All those charged with its conduct reverently observed this grand institution of the state, pledging their hearts and exhausting their strength, none daring to slacken or take their ease. Their efforts to inspire the scholars exceeded those of former times. That the number selected was limited was simply a matter of compliance with the prescribed regulations.
Now that the record is complete, I, Xuekui, having undeservedly occupied the lowest place among those assessing the examination papers, ought to append a preface on its final leaves. Alas! Even scholars unfortunate enough to be born in unfavorable times should resist prevailing customs and strive diligently in their studies…

title: 正德八年河南鄉試錄
text:
冒禁以成身今河南爲萬古
斯文所發之源爲宋程氏兩
夫子所出之地而况接壤
帝畿風化之所漸漑者最先且盛
諸士子幸而生于其鄉又幸
而遭逢其時兹乃賓興而來
隨計而往嚮用髙遠此其擢
===
輿𨗳皆愼始愼終正己正物
相與𤠔成
太平熈洽之治於億萬年也夫
抵科目取士雖以文而主司
所望乎士者不徒以文士之
進身雖以科目而所以自成
其身者不可徒恃乎科目設
punctuated:
冒禁以成身。今河南爲萬古斯文所發之源，爲宋程氏兩夫子所出之地，而况接壤帝畿，風化之所漸漑者最先且盛。諸士子幸而生于其鄉，又幸而遭逢其時，兹乃賓興而來，隨計而往，嚮用髙遠。此其擢輿𨗳皆愼始愼終，正己正物，相與𤠔成太平熈洽之治於億萬年也。
夫抵科目取士雖以文，而主司所望乎士者不徒以文；士之進身雖以科目，而所以自成其身者不可徒恃乎科目。設
translation_en:
…and brave prohibitions to perfect themselves. Now Henan is the source from which this enduring cultural tradition sprang, and the land that produced the two Masters Cheng of the Song dynasty. Moreover, it borders the imperial capital region, receiving the permeating influence of moral transformation earlier and more abundantly than other places. These students are fortunate to have been born in this land, and fortunate also to have encountered this age. Now they come through the ceremonial recommendation of worthy men and depart with the delegation to the capital, their prospects for employment lofty and far-reaching. In their advancement and guidance [?], may they all exercise care at both beginning and end, rectify themselves and others, and together bring about [?] an era of great peace, flourishing harmony, and concord for countless ages.
Generally speaking [?], although the examination system selects men through their writing, those presiding over it expect more from scholars than writing alone. Although scholars advance through the examinations, they cannot rely solely on examinations to perfect themselves. Suppose…

title: 正德八年河南鄉試錄
text:
河南鄉試錄序
我
太祖高皇帝建元洪武之年始定
河洛謂君天下非中州不可
夏四月躬率禁兵泛舟江淮
遡河入汴將擇而居之既而
鼎定金陵不果至而二年三
===
年春免祖之
詔每及兹地九年秋社感侍臣言
猶勤山川與古今人物之思
聖心之拳拳中州者如此
太宗文皇帝北都幽薊亦惟于是
供億之省材勇之惜邉澤之
布必先焉
punctuated:
河南鄉試錄序

我太祖高皇帝建元洪武之年，始定河洛，謂君天下非中州不可。夏四月，躬率禁兵，泛舟江淮，遡河入汴，將擇而居之。既而鼎定金陵，不果至，而二年、三年春，免祖之詔每及兹地。九年秋，社感侍臣言，猶勤山川與古今人物之思。聖心之拳拳中州者如此。

太宗文皇帝北都幽薊，亦惟于是供億之省、材勇之惜、邉澤之布，必先焉。
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Henan Provincial Examination

In the year when our Emperor Taizu Gao inaugurated the Hongwu reign, he first pacified the He–Luo region. He declared that ruling All under Heaven required occupying the Central Region. In the fourth month of summer, he personally led the imperial guard, traveling by boat along the Yangzi and Huai rivers and upstream along the Yellow River into Bian, intending to select a place there as his residence. Subsequently, he established his capital at Jinling and did not ultimately arrive. Yet in the springs of the second and third years, his edicts granting tax remission [?; transcribed as 免祖] invariably extended to this land. In the autumn of the ninth year, moved by the words of an attendant official [?; the transcription 社感 is doubtful], he continued to give earnest thought to its mountains and rivers and its notable figures, past and present. Such was the imperial heart’s devoted concern for the Central Region.

Emperor Taizong Wen established his northern capital in the You–Ji region. He too invariably gave this land priority in reducing provisioning burdens, cherishing talented and valiant men, and extending beneficence to the frontier [?; 邉澤].

title: 正德八年河南鄉試錄
text:
列聖相承世積凞洽百四十餘年
士生其間沾被敎養於兩畿
爲密邇視諸藩爲獨厚激昂
奮發得之相觀令日之人才
殆非
國初比矣科目之所取者其能
盡乎令
===
聖天子即位之八年八月天下當
大比河南廵按監察御史陸
〔鰲〕謹循舊典謟于藩臬預聘
〔賢〕等以柄校文比至如期入
院〔鰲〕職在監臨謂〔賢〕偕學正
王〔學夔〕職考試學正鄧〔鏞〕教
諭楊〔澤〕鄒〔府〕林〔寬〕黃〔永椿〕桑
punctuated:
列聖相承，世積凞洽，百四十餘年。士生其間，沾被敎養，於兩畿爲密邇，視諸藩爲獨厚。激昂奮發，得之相觀，令日之人才，殆非國初比矣。科目之所取者，其能盡乎？
令聖天子即位之八年八月，天下當大比。河南廵按監察御史陸〔鰲〕謹循舊典，謟于藩臬，預聘〔賢〕等以柄校文。比至，如期入院。〔鰲〕職在監臨，謂〔賢〕偕學正王〔學夔〕職考試，學正鄧〔鏞〕、教諭楊〔澤〕、鄒〔府〕、林〔寬〕、黃〔永椿〕、桑
translation_en:
Successive sagely emperors have carried on the succession, and peace and concord have accumulated from generation to generation for more than 140 years. Scholars born during this time have benefited from instruction and nurture. Close to the two metropolitan regions, they have enjoyed particularly generous provision compared with those of the other provinces. Inspired and stirred to exert themselves through observing one another, the talented men of the present day [?] can scarcely be compared with those at the dynasty’s founding. Can selection through the examination system encompass them all?
In the eighth month of the eighth year since the present [?] sagely Son of Heaven ascended the throne, the triennial examination was due throughout the realm. Lu Ao 陸鰲, Regional Inspector of Henan, scrupulously followed established precedent and consulted [?] the Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions, inviting Xian 賢 and others in advance to take charge of evaluating the examination compositions. Upon arrival, they entered the examination compound as scheduled. Ao’s duty was to serve as Supervising Official. He stated that Xian, together with Wang Xuekui 王學夔, an Instructor, would serve as Examiners; Deng Yong 鄧鏞, an Instructor; Yang Ze 楊澤, Zou Fu 鄒府, Lin Kuan 林寬, Huang Yongchun 黃永椿, and Sang, Educational Instructors …

title: 正德八年河南鄉試錄
text:
濟〔邦〕訓導秦〔錡〕職同考試若
提調則右布政使楊〔子器〕左
參政何〔孟春〕監試則按察使
陳〔璘〕副使沙〔鵬〕是職其他執
事皆出懋簡各有專責簾内
外惟公惟慎申飭備至乃合
提學僉事劉〔玉〕所簡士三試
===
之卷冊浩穰展分奎聚文辭
典麗玉映珠聯盛哉河南之
士之文也而
制額限焉拆卷錄名定八十人
而止〔賢〕於
國初額數計之固有以知今日
中州人才之盛于昔也於是
punctuated: 濟〔邦〕、訓導秦〔錡〕職同考試。若提調，則右布政使楊〔子器〕、左參政何〔孟春〕；監試，則按察使陳〔璘〕、副使沙〔鵬〕是職。其他執事皆出懋簡，各有專責。簾内外惟公惟慎，申飭備至。乃合提學僉事劉〔玉〕所簡士三試之卷冊，浩穰，展分奎聚，文辭典麗，玉映珠聯。盛哉，河南之士之文也！而制額限焉，拆卷錄名，定八十人而止。〔賢〕於國初額數計之，固有以知今日中州人才之盛于昔也。於是
translation_en:
…Jibang and Assistant Instructor Qin Qi served as Associate Examiners. The Proctors were Right Provincial Administration Commissioner Yang Ziqi and Left Administration Vice Commissioner He Mengchun. Surveillance Commissioner Chen Lin and Surveillance Vice Commissioner Sha Peng served as examination monitors. All the other functionaries were carefully selected, each with specific responsibilities. Both inside and outside the examination curtain, impartiality and caution alone governed their conduct; instructions and admonitions were thorough in every respect.

We then assembled the booklets from the three examination sessions submitted by the candidates whom Education Intendant Liu Yu, an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner, had selected. They were vast in number, spread out like a gathering of the stars of Kui, the constellation of literary accomplishment [?]. Their language was elegant and classically refined, like gleaming jade and strung pearls. Magnificent indeed were the writings of Henan’s scholars! Yet the imperially prescribed quota imposed a limit. The booklets were unsealed and the names recorded; the final selection stopped at eighty men. Comparing this with the quota at the beginning of the dynasty, I, Xian, can certainly see that talent in Zhongzhou flourishes more abundantly today than in the past. Thereupon…

title: 正德八年河南鄉試錄
text:
錄其在前列者文二十篇餘
文雖美不盡錄錄成當獻諸
上而賢當序諸首簡或曰河南天
地之中古多帝王立國之地
聖賢發跡之區虞夏前世遠
姑弗論詩書所稱若周召之
所治申甫之所生孔孟之所
===
遊萬世一日古不旣盛矣乎
秦漢而下士之以學行名業
顯者未易僂數漢若賈誼有
王佐才唐若韓愈推文章大
家宋若程氏兄弟爲道學眞
儒不亦其中之盛者乎今科
目所取固文也於古里選之
punctuated: 錄其在前列者文二十篇，餘文雖美，不盡錄。錄成，當獻諸上，而賢當序諸首簡。或曰：「河南，天地之中，古多帝王立國之地、聖賢發跡之區。虞夏前世遠，姑弗論。詩書所稱，若周召之所治、申甫之所生、孔孟之所遊，萬世一日，古不旣盛矣乎？秦漢而下，士之以學行名業顯者，未易僂數。漢若賈誼，有王佐才；唐若韓愈，推文章大家；宋若程氏兄弟，爲道學眞儒，不亦其中之盛者乎？今科目所取，固文也，於古里選之
translation_en:
…twenty essays by those ranked foremost were recorded. Although the remaining essays were fine, they were not all included. Once the record was completed, it was to be presented to His Majesty, and I, Xian, was to provide a preface for its opening pages.
Someone said: “Henan lies at the center of Heaven and Earth. In antiquity, it contained many places where emperors and kings established their states and where sages and worthies first rose to prominence. The ages of Yu and Xia are remote; let us leave them aside for now. As for the places mentioned in the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents—those governed by the Dukes of Zhou and Shao, those where Shen and Fu were born, and those visited by Kongzi and Mengzi—their renown endures through ten thousand generations as through a single day. Was this not already a flourishing land in antiquity? From the Qin and Han onward, the scholars distinguished for learning, conduct, reputation, and achievement are too numerous to count readily on one’s fingers. In the Han, Jia Yi possessed the talent to assist a true king; in the Tang, Han Yu was acclaimed as a great master of prose; in the Song, the Cheng brothers were true Confucian scholars of the Learning of the Way. Were these not among its most outstanding figures? What the examinations select for today is certainly literary composition; compared with the ancient method of selection through local communities…”

title: 正德八年河南鄉試錄
text:
法異然有司舍是亦將何所
據依賈誼之通達國體蓋自
其書見之韓愈之第號龍虎
榜重其文也程顥氏試論一
出識者知其有聖賢之學然
則謂科目不足得人文不足
取士也可乎伏惟
===
國家養士學校無非先王三物
之教科目之所取者在是因
言採心即文占行古今之所
不能廢也中州自宋南渡陷
沒金元我
朝始復文明之舊今日之盛豈
非
punctuated: 法異，然有司舍是，亦將何所據依？賈誼之通達國體，蓋自其書見之；韓愈之第，號龍虎榜，重其文也；程顥氏試論一出，識者知其有聖賢之學。然則謂科目不足得人，文不足取士也，可乎？伏惟國家養士學校，無非先王三物之教，科目之所取者在是。因言採心，即文占行，古今之所不能廢也。中州自宋南渡，陷沒金元，我朝始復文明之舊。今日之盛，豈非
translation_en:
…differs from that method. Yet if the responsible officials were to abandon this, what else could they rely upon? Jia Yi’s thorough understanding of statecraft can be discerned from his writings. The examination list on which Han Yu passed was called the “Dragon and Tiger List,” reflecting the esteem accorded his literary work. Once Cheng Hao’s examination discourse appeared, discerning readers knew that he possessed the learning of the sages and worthies. Can one therefore say that examinations cannot obtain worthy men, or that writing cannot serve to select scholars?

I humbly submit that the state nurtures scholars in its schools entirely through the former kings’ teaching of the three categories: virtue, conduct, and skills. These are what the examinations seek in selecting men. To discern the heart through words and judge conduct through writing is something neither antiquity nor the present can dispense with. Since the Song court moved south, Zhongzhou had fallen under Jin and Yuan rule; only under our dynasty was its former cultural refinement restored. Is not the flourishing of the present day …

title: 正德八年河南鄉試錄
text:
祖宗之�François顧而深眷者有以再造
之耶時鎮守太監王〔宏〕自薊
移鎮省城實重是舉巡撫左
副都御史鄧〔璋〕行部方岳之
餘念當試期遂預回鎮稽據
品式凡宜作興視昔加備而
清軍監察御史許〔完〕又奉
===
命當至右叅政胡〔玥〕臧〔鳳〕劉〔顯〕副
使李〔璽〕文〔皓〕左叅議董〔鋭〕右
叅議石〔昭〕僉事陳〔和〕王〔玹〕何
〔正〕王〔納〕誨〔相〕馮〔相〕劉〔文〕寵〔澤〕劉
甯〔河〕曾〔大〕顯〔相〕相與賛襄厥事
務爲
朝廷得人以稱今日之盛其用
punctuated: 祖宗之�François顧而深眷者，有以再造之耶？時鎮守太監王〔宏〕自薊移鎮省城，實重是舉。巡撫左副都御史鄧〔璋〕行部方岳之餘，念當試期，遂預回鎮，稽據品式，凡宜作興，視昔加備。而清軍監察御史許〔完〕又奉命當至。右叅政胡〔玥〕、臧〔鳳〕、劉〔顯〕，副使李〔璽〕、文〔皓〕，左叅議董〔鋭〕，右叅議石〔昭〕，僉事陳〔和〕、王〔玹〕、何〔正〕、王〔納〕、誨〔相〕、馮〔相〕、劉〔文〕、寵〔澤〕、劉甯〔河〕、曾〔大〕、顯〔相〕，相與賛襄厥事，務爲朝廷得人，以稱今日之盛。其用
translation_en:
…could it be that the ancestors’ regard [?—the transcription is corrupt here] and profound solicitude had brought about this renewal?

At this time, the Regional Defender, Grand Eunuch Wang Hong, had transferred his station from Ji to the provincial capital and attached great importance to this examination. The Grand Coordinator and Left Vice Censor-in-Chief, Deng Zhang, mindful that the examination season was approaching, returned to his station in advance after touring the region.
