考試官教授陸　批〔作表之法忌排忌事余忌夫平仄〕
===
正議大夫守尚書左僕射兼門下侍郎臣
光稽首頓首上言伏惟堯舜之事載于典
謨循之可以致治文武之政布在方策舉
之存乎得人歷觀既往之盛衰足為將來
之勸戒切念臣酷嗜史學每厭繁文通志
脩而卷帙猶多敘述詳而檢閱難徧乃自
punctuated:
可以開智牖，可以升孔子之堂而入其室矣。謹論。

表
擬宋司馬光進稽古錄表〔元祐元年〕
車富

同考試官教諭楊批〔司馬公進稽古錄表自有手筆〕：此篇擬之，頗相類。
同考試官學正鄧批〔駢儷有則亦非不能為四六者〕。
考試官學正王批〔字字句句着實宛然寫出溫公〕：頗悉君父之志。此作甚得體。
考試官教授陸批〔作表之法忌排忌事余忌夫平仄〕。

正議大夫、守尚書左僕射兼門下侍郎臣光，稽首頓首上言：伏惟堯舜之事，載于典謨，循之可以致治；文武之政，布在方策，舉之存乎得人。歷觀既往之盛衰，足為將來之勸戒。切念臣酷嗜史學，每厭繁文。通志脩而卷帙猶多，敘述詳而檢閱難徧。乃自
translation_en:
…one may open the window of wisdom, ascend into Confucius’s hall, and enter his inner chamber. Respectfully submitted as a discourse.

Memorial
A memorial modeled on Sima Guang of the Song presenting the Record of Investigations into Antiquity (Jigu lu)〔First year of Yuanyou, 1086〕
By Che Fu.

Associate Examiner Yang, Instructor, comments: 〔Master Sima’s own memorial presenting the Record of Investigations into Antiquity survives in his writing.〕 This piece imitates it quite closely.
Associate Examiner Deng, Instructor, comments: 〔The parallel phrasing follows proper rules; this writer is certainly capable of composing four-six prose.〕
Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: 〔Every word and sentence has substance, vividly recreating the Duke of Wen, Sima Guang.〕 It shows considerable understanding of the intentions of the sovereign and father. This composition is most fitting in form and manner.
Examiner Lu, Professor, comments: 〔In composing memorials, one should avoid excessive parallel arrangement and allusions [?]; I avoid the constraints of level and oblique tones [?].〕

Your servant Guang, Grand Master for Correct Counsel, serving as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and concurrently Vice Director of the Chancellery, bows his head to the ground and repeatedly kowtows, submitting these words: I humbly reflect that the deeds of Yao and Shun are recorded in the Canons and Counsels; by following them, good government may be achieved. The policies of Kings Wen and Wu are set forth in the written records; putting them into practice depends upon obtaining the right men. A comprehensive examination of past flourishing and decline can provide encouragement and admonition for the future. I earnestly reflect that I, your servant, have an intense fondness for historical learning and have often found prolix writing wearisome. Although the Comprehensive Record (Tongzhi) had been compiled, its volumes remained numerous; although its narrative was detailed, it was difficult to consult it throughout. Therefore, beginning with…

title: 正德八年河南鄉試錄
text:
羲農以入戰國由秦漢以至
本朝上下幾四千年記纂纔二十卷倣春秋
之筆削愧乏三長竭旦暮之劬勞較有一
得恭遇
○○○
繼離出震
旋乾轉坤纘
太祖太宗之基圖而負荷不墜承
太皇太后之佑啓而孝養不違
===
式尚典刑
延登耆舊〔臣〕已廢復起既老且衰扶病趨
班豈堪重任捐軀報
國用畢愚誠凡今日所當盡之心皆平生可
對人之語冒陳鄙拙仰荅
恩私伏願
明目達聰改新法而竟除四害隱惡揚善察
邇言而試用五規力回慶曆之徽風無蹈
熙豐之覆轍〔臣〕無任懇切願望戰汗屏營
punctuated: 羲農以入戰國，由秦漢以至本朝，上下幾四千年，記纂纔二十卷。倣春秋之筆削，愧乏三長；竭旦暮之劬勞，較有一得。恭遇○○○，繼離出震，旋乾轉坤，纘太祖太宗之基圖而負荷不墜，承太皇太后之佑啓而孝養不違，式尚典刑，延登耆舊。〔臣〕已廢復起，既老且衰，扶病趨班，豈堪重任？捐軀報國，用畢愚誠。凡今日所當盡之心，皆平生可對人之語。冒陳鄙拙，仰荅恩私。伏願明目達聰，改新法而竟除四害；隱惡揚善，察邇言而試用五規。力回慶曆之徽風，無蹈熙豐之覆轍。〔臣〕無任懇切願望、戰汗屏營
translation_en:
…from Fuxi and Shennong into the Warring States period, and from the Qin and Han down to our present dynasty: a span of nearly four thousand years, compiled into just twenty fascicles. I have imitated the editorial judgments of the Spring and Autumn Annals, though ashamed to lack the historian’s three strengths. Exhausting myself in labor from dawn to dusk, I have nevertheless achieved something of worth.

I respectfully have the good fortune to serve ○○○ [?], who has succeeded to the throne’s radiance and emerged to rule, turning Heaven and Earth; who carries forward the foundations and grand designs of Taizu and Taizong, bearing this burden without letting it fall; who receives the Grand Empress Dowager’s protection and guidance, never failing in filial care; and who honors established models and promotes venerable, experienced men. Your servant, once dismissed, has been recalled, but is now both old and infirm. Struggling through illness to attend the ranks at court, how could I bear weighty responsibilities? Yet I would give my life to repay the state, exhausting my humble sincerity. Everything I ought now to express with all my heart consists of words I could openly speak before others throughout my life. I venture to present this crude work in grateful response to your personal favor.

I humbly pray that you will open your eyes and ears to all, revise the New Policies and completely eliminate the four harms; conceal faults and commend virtues, examine even ordinary remarks and try putting the five admonitions into practice. Strive to restore the admirable customs of the Qingli era, and do not repeat the disastrous course of the Xining and Yuanfeng eras. Your servant cannot contain his earnest hopes and wishes, trembling, sweating, and anxious…

title: 正德八年河南鄉試錄
text:
之至謹以所撰稽古錄隨
表上
進以
聞
第叁場
策
第一問
同考試官教諭黄　批　李茂元
〔堯言布天下宜人人能誦之〕
〔而心法一書士子知者蓋鮮此策獨能敷對無遺篇終所以自獻又〕
===
聖訓中數語而忠愛宛至他日
不出
經筵進講吾有望於子矣
同考試官教諭鄒　批　〔心法一書擬〕
文皇所以繼聖學而傳之
聖子神孫以開太平於萬世者其洪綱要旨
御製序文昭示甚悉他若在昔聖賢格言於四卷中又悉載矣今日有司之意不過欲
敷揚
punctuated:
之至。謹以所撰《稽古錄》隨表上進以聞。
第叁場
策
第一問
同考試官教諭黄批，李茂元。
〔堯言布天下，宜人人能誦之。〕〔而心法一書，士子知者蓋鮮。此策獨能敷對無遺，篇終所以自獻又〕聖訓中數語，而忠愛宛至。他日不出經筵進講，吾有望於子矣。
同考試官教諭鄒批：〔心法一書，擬〕文皇所以繼聖學而傳之聖子神孫，以開太平於萬世者。其洪綱要旨，御製序文昭示甚悉。他若在昔聖賢格言，於四卷中又悉載矣。今日有司之意，不過欲敷揚
translation_en:
…to the utmost. I respectfully submit the Record of Examining Antiquity (Jigu lu), which I have compiled, together with this memorial for Your Majesty’s attention.
Third Session
Policy Essays
First Question
Comment by Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor, on the essay of Li Maoyuan:
〔The words of Yao are disseminated throughout the realm; everyone ought to be able to recite them.〕〔Yet few examination candidates know the book Methods of the Mind (Xinfa). This policy essay alone sets forth a complete response, leaving nothing out. The offering made at its conclusion also〕 consists of several phrases from the sage instructions [?], yet its loyalty and devotion are movingly expressed. In days to come, without going beyond lecturing at the Classics Colloquium [?], you may fulfill the hopes I place in you.
Comment by Associate Examiner Zou, Instructor:
〔The book Methods of the Mind, modeled on [?]〕 was the means by which Emperor Wen continued the learning of the sages and transmitted it to his sagely sons and divine grandsons, to inaugurate great peace for all generations. Its broad principles and essential purport are most fully explained in the imperially composed preface. Moreover, the exemplary sayings of the sages and worthies of former times are all recorded in its four fascicles. The intention of the responsible officials today was merely to expound and proclaim…

title: 正德八年河南鄉試錄
text:
聖謨以仰稗
聖德而塲中荅者乃茫無所知篇終之獻往往别爲一說徐而觀之亦老生之常談耳此策不
然其能那膺
祖訓者歟
考試官學正王　批
天法
祖勤政用人謹好惡辨邪正明賞罰繼世而有天下者脩德保位之大端也
故
文皇於心法序中必𣈆天心人心君心言之此策能悉以陳而謂
==
==
==
===
今日之所要者急者在是可謂能仰識
聖心者矣録之庶有所藉以達于吾
聖天子
考試官教授陸　批　於
聖製中及心字者敷陳蓋矣非留心
聖學之士何能如此
帝王之治出於道而道不外乎心帝王之
學原於心而心不離乎道蓋道者治之本
也必心以爲之歸宿外乎心則治不出於
punctuated:
聖謨，以仰稗聖德，而塲中荅者乃茫無所知，篇終之獻往往别爲一說。徐而觀之，亦老生之常談耳。此策不然，其能那膺祖訓者歟？
考試官學正王批：天法祖，勤政用人，謹好惡，辨邪正，明賞罰，繼世而有天下者脩德保位之大端也。故文皇於《心法》序中必𣈆天心、人心、君心言之。此策能悉以陳，而謂今日之所要者、急者在是，可謂能仰識聖心者矣。録之，庶有所藉以達于吾聖天子。
考試官教授陸批：於聖製中及心字者，敷陳蓋矣。非留心聖學之士，何能如此？
帝王之治出於道，而道不外乎心；帝王之學原於心，而心不離乎道。蓋道者，治之本也，必心以爲之歸宿；外乎心，則治不出於
translation_en:
…the imperial counsels, thereby assisting [?] imperial virtue. Yet those answering in the examination hall understood nothing of this; the recommendations at the ends of their essays frequently pursued some other argument. On closer examination, these were merely the usual platitudes of old scholars. This policy essay is different. Might its author be capable of receiving and upholding [?] the ancestral instructions?
Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: Taking Heaven as a model [?] and emulating the ancestors, attending diligently to government and employing men, exercising care in likes and dislikes, distinguishing the depraved from the upright, and making rewards and punishments clear—these are the principal means by which one who inherits rule over the realm cultivates virtue and preserves his position. Thus, in his preface to Methods of the Mind, Emperor Wen necessarily discusses [?] Heaven’s mind, the people’s minds, and the ruler’s mind. This policy essay sets all these out fully and declares that herein lie the essential and urgent needs of the present day. Its author may indeed be said to understand the imperial mind reverently. We record it in the hope that there may thereby be a means of conveying it to our sage Son of Heaven.
Examiner Lu, Professor, comments: The passages in the imperial composition that touch upon the word “mind” have been fully expounded. How could anyone accomplish this without devoting attention to the learning of the sages?
The government of emperors and kings proceeds from the Way, and the Way does not lie outside the mind. The learning of emperors and kings originates in the mind, and the mind is inseparable from the Way. For the Way is the foundation of government and must find its ultimate resting place in the mind. Outside the mind, government does not proceed from…

title: 正德八年河南鄉試錄
text:
道矣心者學之源也必道以爲之主宰離
乎道則學不原於心矣治不出於道既無
其本雖有小小之補塞不足以稱治學不
原於心既無其源雖極區區之探討不足
以成學此我
太宗文皇帝聖學心法一書之所由輯而有以
繼往聖之絕學以開
今日之盛治也愚嘗伏讀
高皇聖諭有曰帝王莫盛於堯舜然觀其授受
===
在允執厥中
文皇聖諭亦曰堯舜相傳允執厥中便是爲治
大哉
王言一哉
王心舜之所受於堯而益之三言以授禹者心
法首載之矣豈非即我
祖宗之所爲授受者歟是書所集皆聖賢之言
文皇自謂於正心脩身齊家治國平天下之要
道大畧已見其于孔氏之書微詞奥旨類
punctuated: 道矣。心者，學之源也，必道以爲之主宰，離乎道則學不原於心矣。治不出於道，既無其本，雖有小小之補塞，不足以稱治；學不原於心，既無其源，雖極區區之探討，不足以成學。此我太宗文皇帝《聖學心法》一書之所由輯，而有以繼往聖之絕學，以開今日之盛治也。愚嘗伏讀高皇聖諭，有曰：「帝王莫盛於堯舜，然觀其授受，在允執厥中。」文皇聖諭亦曰：「堯舜相傳，允執厥中，便是爲治。」大哉，王言！一哉，王心！舜之所受於堯，而益之三言以授禹者，《心法》首載之矣。豈非即我祖宗之所爲授受者歟？是書所集，皆聖賢之言。文皇自謂：「於正心、脩身、齊家、治國、平天下之要道，大畧已見。」其于孔氏之書，微詞奥旨，類
translation_en:
…the Way. The mind is the source of learning, and the Way must govern it; apart from the Way, learning does not originate in the mind. If government does not issue from the Way, it lacks its foundation: even minor repairs and remedies do not suffice to qualify it as good government. If learning does not originate in the mind, it lacks its source: even the utmost narrow inquiry does not suffice to constitute true learning. This is why our Emperor Wen, Taizong, compiled Methods of the Mind in Sagely Learning (Shengxue xinfa): to carry forward the interrupted learning of the sages of old and inaugurate the flourishing government of today.
I have reverently read a sacred instruction of Emperor Gao which says: “Among emperors and kings, none surpassed Yao and Shun. Yet when we consider what they transmitted and received, it lay in ‘truly holding fast to the Mean.’” A sacred instruction of Emperor Wen likewise says: “What Yao and Shun transmitted to one another—‘truly holding fast to the Mean’—is precisely what governing consists in.” How great are these royal words! How united are these royal minds! What Shun received from Yao, and augmented with three further injunctions before transmitting it to Yu, is recorded at the very beginning of Methods of the Mind. Is this not precisely what our imperial ancestors themselves transmitted and received? Everything collected in this book consists of the words of sages and worthies. Emperor Wen himself said: “The essentials of rectifying the mind, cultivating the person, ordering the family, governing the state, and bringing peace to all under Heaven are broadly set forth here.” As for the subtle expressions and profound meanings in the writings of Confucius, generally …

title: 正德八年河南鄉試錄
text:
從乘錄統言專言之間綱提目舉寧復有
遺憾乎今
御製序文具在序括諸篇篇爲之釋事必求道
言必原心論天而必反諸躬取人而必考
諸己丹青炳煥歷世弗渝雲漢昭回有目
同仰所謂萬事根於一心先明諸心使無
毫髮之蔽裁制萬物各得其宜則體周用
備者首是書之旨也所謂天命無常惟德
是與惟能脩德以合天心則天命眷顧久
===
而益隆者終是書之意也而又謂人心之
敬忽有間天命之去留無常者序敬天也
祖宗之法以爲後世當敬守之不可以忽
者序法祖也一心之用周流天地德以服
人宜莫如勤者序勤政也一人之心有好
惡衆人之議合至公者序用人也序謹好
惡則有心之好惡不可不慎茍爲不慎蔽
固溺深之儆序辯邪正則有明君之心公
以正君子之心有所合而偏邪之人無自
punctuated: 從乘錄，統言、專言之間，綱提目舉，寧復有遺憾乎？今御製序文具在，序括諸篇，篇爲之釋，事必求道，言必原心，論天而必反諸躬，取人而必考諸己。丹青炳煥，歷世弗渝；雲漢昭回，有目同仰。所謂「萬事根於一心，先明諸心，使無毫髮之蔽，裁制萬物，各得其宜，則體周用備」者，首是書之旨也。所謂「天命無常，惟德是與，惟能脩德以合天心，則天命眷顧，久而益隆」者，終是書之意也。而又謂「人心之敬忽有間，天命之去留無常」者，序敬天也；「祖宗之法，以爲後世當敬守之，不可以忽」者，序法祖也；「一心之用，周流天地，德以服人，宜莫如勤」者，序勤政也；「一人之心有好惡，衆人之議合至公」者，序用人也。序謹好惡，則有「心之好惡不可不慎，茍爲不慎，蔽固溺深」之儆；序辯邪正，則有「明君之心公以正，君子之心有所合，而偏邪之人無自
translation_en:
…[The opening phrase 從乘錄 is unclear.] In its general statements and its particular discussions, it sets out the main principles and enumerates the particulars: could anything still be lacking? Now the imperially composed preface survives in full. The preface encompasses the chapters, and the chapters explain it. In affairs, it invariably seeks the Way; in words, it invariably traces their source to the mind. When discussing Heaven, it invariably turns back upon oneself; when selecting men, it invariably examines oneself. Brilliant as painted colors, it remains unchanged through successive ages; shining like the Milky Way, it is admired by all who have eyes.

Its statement that “all affairs are rooted in the one mind; first illuminate the mind, allowing not the slightest obscuration, and regulate the myriad things so that each receives its proper treatment: then substance will be complete and function fully provided for” expresses the purport with which this book begins. Its statement that “Heaven’s Mandate is not constant: it supports only virtue; only by cultivating virtue to accord with Heaven’s mind can one receive the favor of Heaven’s Mandate, growing ever greater with time” expresses the intent with which this book ends.

Furthermore, the statement that “the human mind alternates between reverence and negligence, while Heaven’s Mandate is inconstant in departing or remaining” introduces Revering Heaven. The statement that “the laws of the ancestors should be reverently preserved by later generations and must not be neglected” introduces Emulating the Ancestors. The statement that “the workings of the one mind circulate throughout Heaven and Earth; to win men’s submission through virtue, nothing is more fitting than diligence” introduces Diligence in Government. The statement that “one person’s mind has its likes and dislikes, while the deliberations of the many accord with the utmost impartiality” introduces Employing Men. The introduction to Exercising Caution in Likes and Dislikes contains the warning that “one must be cautious about the mind’s likes and dislikes; if one is not cautious, its obscuration becomes entrenched and its immersion deep.” The introduction to Distinguishing the Devious from the Upright contains the statement that “the enlightened ruler’s mind is impartial and upright, so the minds of gentlemen find accord with it, while biased and devious men have no means of…”

title: 正德八年河南鄉試錄
text:
入之論序明賞罰則又有人君以天地爲
心則賞罰必當之說凡此皆所以原心而
求道者也而序之終篇又欲
聖子神孫觀是書者先觀其序以知其用心其
詞旨之丁寧誨諭之詳至舜禹而後實見
于今
列聖相承聿脩厥德誦服是書咸憲以監古訓
有獲四方用靖萬邦作孚於萬斯年受天
之祜所以永
宗社之慶於悠久以無負
皇祖之訓者蓋世有哲王道此一道而心此一
心矣而執事尤以今日之要且急者爲問
豈不以敬
天法
祖勤政用人爲大且要而謹好惡辯邪正明賞
罰又其當急者乎
聖謨洋洋嘉言孔彰歛袵展卷日星在懸老生
之常談愚豈容復贅而天下大器保之最
punctuated:
入之論。序明賞罰，則又有人君以天地爲心，則賞罰必當之說。凡此皆所以原心而求道者也。而序之終篇，又欲聖子神孫觀是書者先觀其序，以知其用心。其詞旨之丁寧、誨諭之詳，至舜禹而後實見于今。
列聖相承，聿脩厥德，誦服是書，咸憲以監。古訓有獲，四方用靖，萬邦作孚，於萬斯年，受天之祜。所以永宗社之慶於悠久，以無負皇祖之訓者，蓋世有哲王，道此一道而心此一心矣。而執事尤以今日之要且急者爲問，豈不以敬天、法祖、勤政、用人爲大且要，而謹好惡、辯邪正、明賞罰又其當急者乎？
聖謨洋洋，嘉言孔彰。歛袵展卷，日星在懸。老生之常談，愚豈容復贅？而天下大器，保之最
translation_en:
…the argument that such people have no means of gaining entry. In introducing the section on making rewards and punishments clear, he further explains that if a ruler takes Heaven and Earth as his own mind, his rewards and punishments will necessarily be fitting. All these teachings seek the Way by tracing matters to their source in the mind. At the end of the preface, he further wishes that his sagely sons and divine grandsons, when reading this book, should first read its preface, so that they may understand his intentions. Such earnestness of expression and fullness of instruction have truly appeared again only now, since the days of Shun and Yu.
The successive sage emperors have continued to cultivate their virtue, reciting and putting this book into practice, all taking it as their model and mirror. Gaining understanding from ancient teachings, they have thereby brought peace to the four quarters and won the trust of the myriad states, receiving Heaven’s blessings for ten thousand years. What perpetuates the blessings of the ancestral temples and the altars of soil and grain into the distant future, without failing the imperial ancestor’s instructions, is surely that each age has a wise king who follows this same Way and makes this same mind his own. Yet you, honored examiners, ask particularly about what is essential and urgent today. Is this not because revering Heaven, emulating the ancestors, diligence in government, and employing worthy men are matters of great and essential importance, while exercising care in likes and dislikes, distinguishing the depraved from the upright, and making rewards and punishments clear are also matters demanding urgent attention?
Vast are the sage counsels; most manifest are their excellent words. Gathering my robes respectfully and opening the volume, I see the sun and stars suspended above. How could I, in my ignorance, presume to add more of an old scholar’s familiar talk? Yet the realm is a great vessel, and preserving it is most …

title: 正德八年河南鄉試錄
text:
難善保則完不善則壞欲不可縱心不可
侈以道制欲以理制心庶幾寡過之訓又
祖宗之所拳拳以致慎於將來者蓋治世之龜
鑑保邦之藥石草茅之賤倘荷收錄獲覲
于
聖天子
經筵之日願隨執事奉此以往謹對
第二問
張景
===
考試官學正王　批〔士之所以能自樹立者以此氣爾子知所以善養而且以不待於人爲大然之論固已可俾末篇集義知命之說又有得於孟氏心法之外者即其所究吾知其他日立〕
朝風采必有可以竦人者矣予其母負主司者之深屬也哉
考試官教授陸　批〔文勢油湧直欲推倒一時豪傑非經學脉使舉子所能及〕
氣之於人也大矣其善養之機由於己而
無所待於人者也夫氣吾氣也人之所同
得而本自浩然者失所養則至於自餒而
punctuated:
難。善保則完，不善則壞。欲不可縱，心不可侈；以道制欲，以理制心，庶幾寡過之訓，又祖宗之所拳拳以致慎於將來者，蓋治世之龜鑑、保邦之藥石。草茅之賤，倘荷收錄，獲覲于聖天子，經筵之日，願隨執事奉此以往。謹對。
第二問
張景
考試官學正王　批〔士之所以能自樹立者，以此氣爾。子知所以善養，而且以不待於人爲大，然之論固已可俾，末篇集義知命之說，又有得於孟氏心法之外者。即其所究，吾知其他日立〕朝，風采必有可以竦人者矣。予其母負主司者之深屬也哉！
考試官教授陸　批〔文勢油湧，直欲推倒一時豪傑，非經學脉使舉子所能及。〕
氣之於人也大矣！其善養之機，由於己而無所待於人者也。夫氣，吾氣也，人之所同得而本自浩然者。失所養，則至於自餒而
translation_en:
…difficult. Preserved well, it remains intact; preserved poorly, it falls into ruin. Desires must not be indulged, nor the heart allowed to grow extravagant. The teaching that one should govern desires through the Way and govern the heart through principle, thereby perhaps committing few errors, is also what the imperial ancestors earnestly enjoined to encourage caution in the future. It is a mirror for governing the age and a remedy for preserving the realm. If I, a humble man of the countryside, should receive the favor of selection and gain an audience with the sagely Son of Heaven, I would wish, on a day of the Classics Colloquium, to accompany you and present these teachings. Respectfully submitted in reply.
Second Question
Zhang Jing
Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: “It is through this vital force (qi) that a scholar can establish himself. You understand how to nourish it well and, moreover, regard independence from others as paramount. This argument is already commendable [?]. The discussion at the end concerning accumulating righteousness and understanding one's allotted destiny also offers insights beyond Mencius's teaching of the heart. Judging from what you have explored, I know that when you one day take your place at court, your bearing will surely command others' awe. May you not disappoint the profound expectations of the official presiding over the examination [?]!”
Examiner Lu, Professor, comments: “The momentum of the writing surges forth, seemingly intent on sweeping aside all the outstanding talents of the age. It is beyond the reach of examination candidates [the phrase concerning classical learning is garbled: ?].”
Great indeed is the importance of vital force to human beings! The means of nourishing it well lie in oneself and depend upon no one else. This vital force is our own: all people alike receive it, and it is originally vast and expansive. If it is not properly nourished, one comes to lose one's inner strength and…

title: 正德八年河南鄉試錄
text:
不能以自拔矣此善養之說所以為聖賢
之大致而學者所當從事也易曰立天之
道曰陰與陽立地之道曰柔與剛立人之
道曰仁與義自夫陰陽剛柔仁義之說立
而世之言氣者異矣天地之間莫非此氣
動直者陽而動闢者剛而流動者剛而
峙立者固剛也發舒者固陽也流動者固亦
仁也力之有強弱者氣禀之不齊養之皆
浩然者體段之本無異爾懦弱邪佞之病
===
固不可以語氣之充而沉靜愿慤之質正
所以為大勇之本也顧世之人歉於義者
不能以自奮而重於得喪者又不免待人
而興焉孟子曰無是餒也又曰豪傑之士
雖無文王猶興噫能知此者寡矣是亦何
惟吾夫子有未見剛者之嘆而孟子以善
養自許哉但其一時問答之詞非已矣之
絕嘆而學者於此自當有以求其實而取
則之也即孔子觀之司寇之位方及七日
punctuated: 不能以自拔矣。此善養之說所以為聖賢之大致，而學者所當從事也。《易》曰：「立天之道曰陰與陽，立地之道曰柔與剛，立人之道曰仁與義。」自夫陰陽剛柔仁義之說立，而世之言氣者異矣。天地之間，莫非此氣。動直者陽，而動闢者剛，而流動者剛，而峙立者固剛也；發舒者固陽也，流動者固亦仁也。力之有強弱者，氣禀之不齊；養之皆浩然者，體段之本無異爾。懦弱邪佞之病，固不可以語氣之充；而沉靜愿慤之質，正所以為大勇之本也。顧世之人，歉於義者不能以自奮，而重於得喪者又不免待人而興焉。孟子曰：「無是，餒也。」又曰：「豪傑之士，雖無文王猶興。」噫！能知此者寡矣。是亦何惟吾夫子有未見剛者之嘆，而孟子以善養自許哉？但其一時問答之詞，非已矣之絕嘆，而學者於此自當有以求其實而取則之也。即孔子觀之，司寇之位方及七日
translation_en: …and cannot extricate themselves. This is why the teaching on properly nurturing qi is a central concern of sages and worthies, and something to which learners must devote themselves. The Book of Changes says: “Establishing the Way of Heaven is called yin and yang; establishing the Way of Earth is called yielding and firm; establishing the Way of humanity is called benevolence and righteousness.” Once this account of yin and yang, yielding and firm, and benevolence and righteousness was established, discussions of qi in the world took on different forms. Between Heaven and Earth, nothing is other than this qi. What moves straight is yang; what moves and opens is firm; what flows is firm; and what stands erect is certainly firm. What unfolds is certainly yang, and what flows is certainly also benevolence [?—the wording of this passage appears garbled]. Differences in strength arise from unequal endowments of qi; that all can nurture it to become vast and overflowing reflects the fundamental sameness of its constitution. The failings of cowardice, perversity, and sycophancy are certainly incompatible with fullness of qi; a disposition of quiet composure, sincerity, and honesty, however, is precisely the foundation of great courage. Yet people in this world who fall short in righteousness cannot rouse themselves, while those who attach great weight to gain and loss inevitably depend on others to stir them to action. Mengzi says: “Without this, it starves.” He also says: “Outstanding men rise to action even without a King Wen.” Alas! Few understand this. Why, then, was it our Master who lamented that he had never seen anyone truly firm, while Mengzi claimed skill in nurturing qi? These were merely words spoken in particular exchanges, not a final sigh of despair that all was over. Learners should therefore seek their substance and take them as a model. Consider Kongzi: he had occupied the office of Minister of Justice for only seven days…

title: 正德八年河南鄉試錄
text:
而誅少正卯者不少遑夾谷之會魯旹蓋岌
岌矣從容數語齊且謝過不暇此其氣何
如也顏子亞明至健而爲邦之問毅然以
王者之事爲已任曾子唯一貫之速而弘
毅之力量尤不可以㑺視他如子夏之謹
嚴子路之勇果固皆有以進乎是曾謂聖
門無剛者乎自夫子有剛之說而養氣之
論獨發於孟子觀其在賓師之位非齊王
所能臣而於公孫衍張儀輩直視之爲妾
===
婦其氣之充要亦無愧於孔子者當時如
告子樂正子之流咸得其一偏而望迹如
魯仲連者亦庶幾矣秦漢而下此風泯泯
間有能存者雖不敢望孔孟之轍差亦足
以扶衰救敝抑邪伸正是皆可與者焉茹
芝如四皓卒能成輔翼之功擊楫如祖逖
猶足發中原之憤一揖而去不克而死其
氣固浩然矣它如李膺諸君子之風節而
漢脉之一綫猶繫楊宻中輩之抗言剴切
punctuated: 而誅少正卯者，不少遑。夾谷之會，魯旹蓋岌岌矣，從容數語，齊且謝過不暇，此其氣何如也？顏子亞明至健，而爲邦之問，毅然以王者之事爲已任。曾子唯一貫之速，而弘毅之力量，尤不可以㑺視。他如子夏之謹嚴、子路之勇果，固皆有以進乎是，曾謂聖門無剛者乎？自夫子有剛之說，而養氣之論獨發於孟子。觀其在賓師之位，非齊王所能臣，而於公孫衍、張儀輩，直視之爲妾婦。其氣之充，要亦無愧於孔子者。當時如告子、樂正子之流，咸得其一偏，而望迹如魯仲連者，亦庶幾矣。秦漢而下，此風泯泯，間有能存者，雖不敢望孔孟之轍，差亦足以扶衰救敝，抑邪伸正，是皆可與者焉。茹芝如四皓，卒能成輔翼之功；擊楫如祖逖，猶足發中原之憤。一揖而去，不克而死，其氣固浩然矣。它如李膺諸君子之風節，而漢脉之一綫猶繫；楊宻中輩之抗言剴切，
translation_en:
…and he executed Shaozheng Mao without the slightest hesitation. At the meeting at Jiagu, Lu was then in grave peril; yet after a few calmly spoken words, Qi could scarcely apologize quickly enough. What strength his vital spirit possessed! Master Yan was next in illumination and supremely firm [?]; when he asked about governing a state, he resolutely took the work of a true king as his own responsibility. Master Zeng promptly assented to the teaching of the single thread running through all [?], and the breadth and resolve of his strength were especially not to be regarded lightly [?]. Others, such as Zixia with his scrupulous gravity and Zilu with his courage and decisiveness, certainly all made progress toward this. Could anyone really claim that the sage’s school had no firm men?

After the Master spoke of firmness, it was Mencius alone who developed the account of nourishing the vital spirit. Consider how, in his position as an honored guest and teacher, he could not be treated as a subject by the king of Qi, while he regarded men such as Gongsun Yan and Zhang Yi simply as concubines and wives. In the fullness of his vital spirit, he was surely worthy of Confucius. Among his contemporaries, men such as Gaozi and Yuezhengzi each grasped one aspect of this; others who followed in his footsteps, such as Lu Zhonglian, also came close.

From the Qin and Han onward, this spirit faded away. Those who occasionally managed to preserve it, although they could not presume to follow in the tracks of Confucius and Mencius, were nevertheless capable of sustaining what was declining, remedying abuses, restraining the crooked, and upholding the upright. All these deserve approval. The Four Hoary Elders, who ate numinous mushrooms, ultimately succeeded in providing support and protection; Zu Ti, who struck his oar in a vow, could still give voice to indignation over the Central Plain. Taking their leave with a bow, or dying before achieving success, their vital spirit was indeed vast and flowing. Likewise, through the moral bearing and integrity of Li Ying and the other gentlemen, the slender thread of the Han dynasty’s life remained intact; and through the forthright, incisive remonstrances of Yang Mizhong [?] and his fellows…

title: 正德八年河南鄉試錄
text:
而當時之奸惡以暴彼豈虞成夫黨錮之
變而求名於編管之禍者哉亦其氣之浩
然而若是焉耳甚矣夫此氣之在人不可
不養也苟以其爲不足以集事而不待養
邪則夫孔孟之爲何往而非氣之充者苟
以其爲有所興起而後可邪則夫士之幼
學壯行者果何事而必待上之人成之春
秋戰國之世亦有作孔孟之氣者在于其
上乎揚子曰周之士也貴秦之士也賤此
===
蓋論世變之說而張子所謂剛則不回柔
則不立者固學者之明戒也學者知所以
自立則無不可爲之事而其所養也充矣
雖然氣之所以充者其功何如也始於義
之能集而有以伸吾之氣終於命之能知
而不沮喪於趨舍進退之正夫然後能以
自立有不待人而興起矣夫士之所以自
任者固宜知此而愚生所論亦惟爲士言
之爾爲人上者顧可聽其自至而不思所
punctuated:
而當時之奸惡以暴。彼豈虞成夫黨錮之變，而求名於編管之禍者哉？亦其氣之浩然而若是焉耳。甚矣夫，此氣之在人不可不養也！苟以其爲不足以集事而不待養邪，則夫孔孟之爲，何往而非氣之充者？苟以其爲有所興起而後可邪，則夫士之幼學壯行者，果何事而必待上之人成之？春秋戰國之世，亦有作孔孟之氣者在于其上乎？揚子曰：「周之士也貴，秦之士也賤。」此蓋論世變之說，而張子所謂「剛則不回，柔則不立」者，固學者之明戒也。學者知所以自立，則無不可爲之事，而其所養也充矣。
雖然，氣之所以充者，其功何如也？始於義之能集，而有以伸吾之氣；終於命之能知，而不沮喪於趨舍進退之正。夫然後能以自立，有不待人而興起矣。夫士之所以自任者，固宜知此，而愚生所論，亦惟爲士言之爾。爲人上者，顧可聽其自至，而不思所
translation_en:
…and thereby the wickedness of that time was exposed. Could they have intended to bring about the calamity of the partisan proscriptions and sought fame through the misfortune of compulsory residence under supervision [?]? It was simply the vastness of their moral vital force (qi) that made them act thus. How essential it is that people nurture this vital force! If one considers it inadequate to accomplish affairs and therefore thinks it need not be nurtured, then in the conduct of Confucius and Mencius, where was there anything that did not express its fullness? If one thinks it can flourish only after something has stirred it into activity, then, for scholars who study in youth and put their learning into practice in maturity, what undertaking must necessarily await fulfillment by those above them? In the Spring and Autumn and Warring States periods, was there anyone above Confucius and Mencius who roused their vital force? Master Yang said: “The scholars of Zhou were honored; the scholars of Qin were held low.” This was a statement about changes in the times. Yet Master Zhang’s saying, “The firm do not bend; the pliant cannot stand,” is indeed a clear admonition to learners. When learners understand how to stand on their own, there is nothing they cannot undertake, and the vital force they nurture becomes full.
Even so, what effort brings this vital force to fullness? It begins with accumulating righteousness, thereby giving scope to one’s vital force; it culminates in understanding Heaven’s mandate, so that one does not become disheartened in rightly choosing what to pursue or set aside, when to advance or withdraw. Only then can one stand on one’s own and rise to action without waiting for others. Scholars ought certainly to understand this as the basis for taking responsibility upon themselves. What I, an ignorant student, have discussed has likewise been addressed solely to scholars. But may those who stand above others simply let them reach this point by themselves, without considering the means …

title: 正德八年河南鄉試錄
text:
以振之乎蓋不有以礪天下之銳則無以
伸天下之氣不有以伸天下之氣則無以
絕天下之佞是故人主以名驅人而以義
激之使天下皆相率以售其直嗚呼是惟
受人之所畏而不甘人之所喜者能之敢
以是爲明問復
第三問
李濂
同考試官訓導秦　批〔記誦多矢本真答問不相對〕
===
同考試官教諭桑　批〔值策場之通弊也此策爲場中最優者故取置前列〕
〔衆言必折諸聖假人必於其倫此古今聽言觀人之法也是作得之〕
考試官學正王　批〔韓周二子人皆知之至其所以爲優劣者則皆未之深考而莫知所適從此篇辨析〕
〔詳盡義理未復槩其爲人而直著其造詣淺深之實以爲立言之本非深有所見不能也〕
考試官教授陸　批〔造詣精當見理分明非聽他人之問而從旁竊記者〕
punctuated:
以振之乎？蓋不有以礪天下之銳，則無以伸天下之氣；不有以伸天下之氣，則無以絕天下之佞。是故人主以名驅人，而以義激之，使天下皆相率以售其直。嗚呼！是惟受人之所畏，而不甘人之所喜者能之。敢以是爲明問復。
第三問
李濂
同考試官訓導秦，批〔記誦多矢本真，答問不相對。〕
同考試官教諭桑，批〔值策場之通弊也。此策爲場中最優者，故取置前列。〕〔衆言必折諸聖，假人必於其倫，此古今聽言觀人之法也。是作得之。〕
考試官學正王，批〔韓周二子，人皆知之。至其所以爲優劣者，則皆未之深考，而莫知所適從。此篇辨析〕〔詳盡，義理未復槩其爲人，而直著其造詣淺深之實，以爲立言之本。非深有所見，不能也。〕
考試官教授陸，批〔造詣精當，見理分明，非聽他人之問而從旁竊記者。〕
translation_en:
…by which to rouse them? For without sharpening the resolve of all under Heaven, there is no way to give full scope to their spirit; without giving full scope to their spirit, there is no way to eradicate their flattery. Thus the ruler impels people through reputation and inspires them through righteousness, so that all under Heaven lead one another in bringing their forthrightness into use. Alas! Only those who accept what others fear and find no relish in what others enjoy can accomplish this. I venture to offer this in reply to your discerning question.
Third Policy Question
Li Lian
Associate Examiner Qin, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔Much memorized material, with the essential truth lost [?]; the answer does not correspond to the question.〕
Associate Examiner Sang, Instructor, comments: 〔This encounters [?] a common failing in the policy examination. This policy essay is the best in the examination, and so it has been selected for placement among the leading entries.〕〔All statements must be judged against the sages; in appraising [?] a person, one must compare him with his peers. This has been the method, past and present, for assessing statements and observing people. This composition grasps it.〕
Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: 〔Everyone knows the two masters Han and Zhou. Yet as to the grounds for judging their relative merits, people have not examined these deeply and do not know whom to follow. This essay’s analysis〕〔is detailed and exhaustive. Its treatment of moral principle does not merely characterize the men in general [?], but directly reveals the actual depth or shallowness of their attainments, making this the basis of its argument. Without profound insight, this could not be achieved.〕
Examiner Lu, Professor, comments: 〔The writer’s attainments are refined and sound, and his understanding of principle is clear. This is not the work of someone who listens to others’ questions [?] and furtively takes notes from the sidelines.〕

title: 正德八年河南鄉試錄
text:
聽言者必揆諸理而後可以爲折衷之準
觀人者必論其世而後可以盡擬倫之公
夫疑似之說不可以易辯而優劣之實不
可以輕議也即言而擬人者不以理揆固
無所據以爲是非之決不以世論亦何所
徵以極知言之道也哉執事發策及於周
韓二子而欲得其所以爲從違者承學生
晚而敢輕爲之說邪惟知言之功爲格致
之始事而尚友之道又取正之大端恭承
===
之下則亦不能以默無所請矣韓子起於
八代文衰之後其所著原道讀荀等篇皆
欲以明乎道者其言曰孟氏醇乎醇者也
又曰荀與揚也擇焉而不精語焉而不詳
夫自孟氏沒道學不傳而尊孟氏之說者
甚鮮愈獨出而尊信之可謂難矣程子謂
其千餘年後斷得分明者正謂此爾周子
生於千載道喪之時特作太極一圖正所
以落夫學者其圖之說曰無極而太極又
punctuated:
聽言者必揆諸理，而後可以爲折衷之準；觀人者必論其世，而後可以盡擬倫之公。夫疑似之說不可以易辯，而優劣之實不可以輕議也。即言而擬人者，不以理揆，固無所據以爲是非之決；不以世論，亦何所徵以極知言之道也哉？執事發策及於周韓二子，而欲得其所以爲從違者，承學生晚，而敢輕爲之說邪？惟知言之功爲格致之始事，而尚友之道又取正之大端，恭承之下，則亦不能以默無所請矣。

韓子起於八代文衰之後，其所著《原道》《讀荀》等篇，皆欲以明乎道者。其言曰：「孟氏醇乎醇者也。」又曰：「荀與揚也，擇焉而不精，語焉而不詳。」夫自孟氏沒，道學不傳，而尊孟氏之說者甚鮮，愈獨出而尊信之，可謂難矣。程子謂其千餘年後斷得分明者，正謂此爾。周子生於千載道喪之時，特作太極一圖，正所以落夫學者。其圖之說曰：「無極而太極。」又
translation_en:
Those who listen to statements must measure them against principle before they can establish a standard for adjudication; those who assess people must consider the age in which they lived before they can achieve complete fairness in comparing them. Seemingly plausible assertions cannot be readily distinguished, and actual superiority or inferiority cannot be lightly judged. When assessing people through their words, without measuring them against principle one certainly has no basis for deciding right and wrong; without considering their age, what evidence could one adduce to attain a full understanding of their words? Your policy question concerns the two masters, Zhou and Han, and seeks the grounds for accepting or rejecting their views. How could I, a late-born student [?], venture lightly to pronounce upon them? Yet understanding words is the first task in investigating things and extending knowledge, while befriending worthy men of antiquity is also a principal means of finding a correct standard. Having respectfully received your question, I cannot remain silent without offering an inquiry.

Master Han emerged after literary writing had declined through eight dynasties. His essays, including Inquiry into the Way (Yuan Dao) and Reading Xunzi (Du Xun), all sought to clarify the Way. He said: “Master Meng was purest of the pure.” He also said: “Xun and Yang selected, but without precision; they spoke, but without thoroughness.” After Master Meng died, learning concerning the Way ceased to be transmitted, and very few honored his teachings. Han Yu alone came forward to honor and trust them: this may indeed be called difficult. Master Cheng’s statement that, more than a thousand years later, Han had reached a clear judgment refers precisely to this. Master Zhou was born when the Way had been lost for a thousand years. He specially composed a Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate, precisely as a means to guide students [?; the transcription reads 落]. His explanation of the diagram says: “Without ultimate, yet the Supreme Ultimate.” He further …

title: 正德八年河南鄉試錄
text:
曰太極本無極夫自孔子有太極之說未
有言無極者而周子獨得而指言之可謂
精矣朱子謂其不由師傳默契道體者正
謂是爾夫即韓子之說固亦若有所得而
傑出於諸家者但其以學文爲第一義則
不免於牽制詞章之習而周子之學性諸
天成諸己上接洙泗千載之統下啓河洛
百世之傳固非韓之所得而並矣或乃疑
其言之相當而無所於從違彼固未揆諸
===
理而槩視之爾原道以博愛爲仁不免遺
體而通書之所謂愛曰仁者蓋別其用而
因以名體也於大學言誠意正心而不及
致知格物是爲無本而通書所謂守之貴
行之利者蓋承仁義中正而言本末之序
亦明矣人性本無不善原性分以爲三品
其說固差彼剛柔善惡中之說則指氣禀
而反之者言此豈愈之所能識也鬼神不
過一氣原鬼以土石風霆與之對言尤爲
punctuated: 曰：「太極本無極。」夫自孔子有太極之說，未有言無極者，而周子獨得而指言之，可謂精矣。朱子謂其不由師傳、默契道體者，正謂是爾。夫即韓子之說，固亦若有所得而傑出於諸家者，但其以學文爲第一義，則不免於牽制詞章之習。而周子之學，性諸天，成諸己，上接洙泗千載之統，下啓河洛百世之傳，固非韓之所得而並矣。或乃疑其言之相當，而無所於從違，彼固未揆諸理而槩視之爾。《原道》以博愛爲仁，不免遺體，而《通書》之所謂「愛曰仁」者，蓋別其用而因以名體也。於《大學》言誠意正心，而不及致知格物，是爲無本，而《通書》所謂「守之貴，行之利」者，蓋承仁義中正而言，本末之序亦明矣。人性本無不善，《原性》分以爲三品，其說固差。彼剛柔善惡中之說，則指氣禀而反之者言，此豈愈之所能識也？鬼神不過一氣，《原鬼》以土石風霆與之對言，尤爲
translation_en: …says: “The Supreme Ultimate is fundamentally without polarity.” Since Confucius put forward the teaching of the Supreme Ultimate, no one had spoken of the absence of polarity; Master Zhou alone grasped this and explicitly stated it. His insight may be called penetrating indeed. Master Zhu’s statement that he silently apprehended the substance of the Way without receiving instruction from a teacher refers precisely to this. Master Han’s teachings, to be sure, likewise seem to contain insights that set him above the various other thinkers. Yet because he regarded the study of literary composition as the foremost concern, he could not escape being constrained by the habits of literary craftsmanship. Master Zhou’s learning, by contrast, was endowed by Heaven and perfected within himself. It reached back to continue the thousand-year tradition of the Zhu and Si Rivers and opened the way for a hundred generations of transmission in the He and Luo region. What Han attained certainly could not equal it. Some, however, remain uncertain, thinking their statements comparable and unable to decide which to follow or reject. Such people have simply viewed them indiscriminately without weighing them against principle. Inquiry into the Way defines benevolence as universal love, thereby inevitably neglecting its substance. The statement in the Comprehensive Writings that “love is called benevolence,” however, distinguishes its function and uses that function to name its substance. In discussing the Great Learning, Han speaks of making the intentions sincere and rectifying the mind, but does not address extending knowledge and investigating things; his account thus lacks a foundation. The Comprehensive Writings speaks of “the value of holding fast to them and the benefit of putting them into practice,” continuing its discussion of benevolence, righteousness, centrality, and correctness. The order of root and branches is thus also clear. Human nature is originally without anything that is not good, yet Inquiry into Human Nature divides it into three grades: its teaching is certainly mistaken. Master Zhou’s discussion of firmness, softness, goodness, evil, and the mean, however, concerns the endowment of vital energy and the restoration of that endowment to its proper state. How could Han Yu have understood this? Ghosts and spirits are nothing beyond the single vital energy, yet Inquiry into Ghosts sets earth, stones, wind, and thunder in opposition to them, which is especially …

title: 正德八年河南鄉試錄
text:
不經彼神妙萬物之說則以不滯於有無
而論此豈愈之所能知也蓋愈之資才甚
高而因文見道是以無窮究精察之實而
周子之書不盡言圖不盡意蓋脉絡分明
而規模宏遠矣是其優劣固不待辨而謂
其言之大畧相當者不已過乎執事猶以
爲所優者乃在於人而不在於言夫即其
言而考其行韓子之爲人也其平居則不
過酣飲博奕之樂其自負則止惟功名進
===
取之念其排佛老之功未有而於潮州之
寂寞乃遂變其處禍福死生之際若謝潮
州表及張籍侑奠之詞則有愧於異學之
流甚多是其見道不精而徒用力於言語
文字之間者矣周子聞道甚早信古好義
胷次洒落而光風霽月之趣可挹遇事剛
果而玉色金聲之著尤毅其家甚約而其
意甚適其取名甚短而希世徼福之念甚
薄蓋其析之有以極其精而不亂合之有
punctuated:
不經。彼神妙萬物之說，則以不滯於有無而論，此豈愈之所能知也？蓋愈之資才甚高，而因文見道，是以無窮究精察之實。而周子之書不盡言，圖不盡意，蓋脉絡分明，而規模宏遠矣。是其優劣固不待辨，而謂其言之大畧相當者，不已過乎？執事猶以爲所優者乃在於人，而不在於言。夫即其言而考其行，韓子之爲人也，其平居則不過酣飲博奕之樂，其自負則止惟功名進取之念，其排佛老之功未有，而於潮州之寂寞乃遂變。其處禍福死生之際，若《謝潮州表》及張籍侑奠之詞，則有愧於異學之流甚多。是其見道不精，而徒用力於言語文字之間者矣。

周子聞道甚早，信古好義，胷次洒落，而光風霽月之趣可挹；遇事剛果，而玉色金聲之著尤毅。其家甚約，而其意甚適；其取名甚短，而希世徼福之念甚薄。蓋其析之有以極其精而不亂，合之有
translation_en:
…contrary to the canonical teachings. By contrast, the account of the spiritual power that wondrously transforms the myriad things proceeds without becoming bound to either existence or nonexistence. How could Yu have understood this? Han Yu’s natural gifts were very great, but he perceived the Way through literary composition; hence he lacked the substance of exhaustive inquiry and precise scrutiny. Master Zhou’s writings do not exhaust what can be said, nor does his diagram exhaust its meaning; yet their underlying connections are clear, and their scope is vast and far-reaching. Which is superior and which inferior surely needs no argument. Is it not mistaken, then, to say that their statements are broadly equivalent? You nevertheless maintain that the superiority lies in the person rather than in his words. Now, if we examine his conduct in light of his words, Master Han’s character becomes apparent. In everyday life, he sought no more than the pleasures of heavy drinking and games of chance and skill; his ambitions extended only to achievement, reputation, and advancement. He had accomplished nothing in his opposition to Buddhism and Daoism, and amid the isolation of Chaozhou he then changed his position. As for his conduct when confronted with misfortune and good fortune, death and life—as seen in his Memorial of Thanks from Chaozhou and Zhang Ji’s words accompanying sacrificial offerings—he had much to be ashamed of even in comparison with followers of heterodox teachings. His perception of the Way was imprecise, and he merely expended his efforts on language and literary composition.

Master Zhou heard the Way very early. He trusted antiquity and cherished righteousness. His heart was open and untroubled, allowing one to savor a quality like a clear breeze and the moon after rain. In dealing with affairs he was firm and decisive; the manifest qualities of jade’s luster and metal’s resonance were especially resolute in him. His household was very poor, yet his mind was thoroughly at ease. His pursuit of reputation was very limited [?], and he had little inclination to court worldly favor or seek blessings. For when he analyzed things, he could reach their utmost subtlety without confusion; when he brought them together, he had the means to…

title: 正德八年河南鄉試錄
text:
以盡其大而無餘則夫推明究極之精而
有以盡其藴者固其所也决以其人大致
又相遠如此然則學者之所從違復何待
於他考而後爲準哉雖然韓子特不及周
子爾秦漢而下至於隋唐異端之說盛行
而正學蕪矣愈獨推尊孟氏發明王道而
自託於不得其傳之後使天下復知有正
學者誰之力也嗚呼愈豈可少也哉謹對
第四問
===
吳瀚
同考試官教諭楊　批〔此策中答此策者往往掇拾源流至論之緒餘而敷衍成篇殊無可人意者此荅有考據有折衷而〕
〔詞簡理明蓋不可以科舉文字視之也〕
同考試官學正鄧　批〔此策不難於荅而難於斷〕
〔制觀子之荅有斷制必有用之才矣〕
考試官學正王　批〔議論平正詞氣雍容比於騁浮〕
〔華以倖一得者遠矣〕
考試官教授陸　批〔典實之作恭之前三場皆稱故〕
punctuated:
以盡其大而無餘，則夫推明究極之精而有以盡其藴者，固其所也。决以其人大致，又相遠如此，然則學者之所從違，復何待於他考而後爲準哉？雖然，韓子特不及周子爾。秦漢而下，至於隋唐，異端之說盛行，而正學蕪矣。愈獨推尊孟氏，發明王道，而自託於不得其傳之後。使天下復知有正學者，誰之力也？嗚呼！愈豈可少也哉？謹對。

第四問
吳瀚

同考試官教諭楊，批〔此策中，答此策者往往掇拾源流至論之緒餘，而敷衍成篇，殊無可人意者。此荅有考據，有折衷，而〕〔詞簡理明，蓋不可以科舉文字視之也。〕

同考試官學正鄧，批〔此策不難於荅，而難於斷〕〔制。觀子之荅，有斷制，必有用之才矣。〕

考試官學正王，批〔議論平正，詞氣雍容，比於騁浮〕〔華以倖一得者，遠矣。〕

考試官教授陸，批〔典實之作，恭之前三場皆稱，故〕
translation_en:
…to encompass its full scope without leaving anything out. Thus, elucidating and pursuing its subtleties to the utmost, so as to exhaust its profundities, was certainly within his capacity. Judged by the general character of the men themselves, they were also so far apart. What further investigation, then, need students await before establishing a standard for what to follow and what to reject? Nevertheless, Master Han was merely inferior to Master Zhou. From the Qin and Han down through the Sui and Tang, heterodox teachings flourished, while orthodox learning fell into neglect. Han Yu alone exalted Master Meng, elucidated the Way of the Kings, and placed himself among those who came after its transmission had been lost. Through whose efforts did the world once again know that orthodox learning existed? Alas! Could Han Yu possibly be dispensed with? I respectfully submit this reply.

Fourth Question
Wu Han

Associate Examiner Yang, Instructor, comments: “Among these policy essays [?], those answering this question have often picked up leftover scraps from the Penetrating Discourses on Origins and Developments (Yuanliu zhilun) and expanded them into an essay; scarcely any have been satisfactory. This answer offers documentary evidence and judicious evaluation, while its language is concise and its reasoning clear. Surely it cannot be regarded as merely examination writing.”

Associate Examiner Deng, School Instructor, comments: “The difficulty of this policy question lies not in answering it but in reaching a firm judgment. Your answer shows such judgment; you must possess talents suited to practical service.”

Examiner Wang, School Instructor, comments: “The discussion is balanced and sound, and the language and tone composed and dignified. It far surpasses the work of those who parade superficial ornament in hopes of a lucky success.”

Examiner Lu, Professor, comments: “A work grounded in authoritative sources and solid facts. Gong [?] performed commendably in all three preceding sessions, therefore…”

title: 正德八年河南鄉試錄
text:
取之
養士於學校則行業專而無他岐之惑取
士於貢舉則趨向正而絕倖進之途此實
求賢之要術圖治之良規也是以治天下
者必以此爲當務之急焉甚矣賢才之有
益於人國然則當何如其作興長育而後
得其用邪古昔盛時陶和毓粹人之所以
自負者甚厚而其所以自進者甚重有不
待於學校之所養貢舉之所取也三代以
===
來上有以求于其下下有所待于其上然
黨庠遂序之法行鄉舉里選之法立而成
周致治亦由於是我
朝倣古爲治用人之效其盛矣乎愚生有志
用世久矣而無由自達茲因執事所問試
一言之周室之季諸侯之士歲不以獻故
子產有不毀鄉校之議而學校之教無傳
焉嬴秦之後智謀之士各逞其雄故漢高
有不事詩書之失而學校之教無聞焉觀
punctuated:
取之。

養士於學校，則行業專而無他岐之惑；取士於貢舉，則趨向正而絕倖進之途。此實求賢之要術、圖治之良規也。是以治天下者，必以此爲當務之急焉。甚矣，賢才之有益於人國！然則當何如其作興長育，而後得其用邪？古昔盛時，陶和毓粹，人之所以自負者甚厚，而其所以自進者甚重，有不待於學校之所養、貢舉之所取也。三代以來，上有以求于其下，下有所待于其上。然黨庠遂序之法行，鄉舉里選之法立，而成周致治亦由於是。我朝倣古爲治，用人之效，其盛矣乎！愚生有志用世久矣，而無由自達。茲因執事所問，試一言之。周室之季，諸侯之士歲不以獻，故子產有不毀鄉校之議，而學校之教無傳焉。嬴秦之後，智謀之士各逞其雄，故漢高有不事詩書之失，而學校之教無聞焉。觀
translation_en:
…selected him.

When scholars are nurtured in schools, their conduct and studies remain focused, free from the confusion of divergent paths; when scholars are selected through recommendation and examination, their aspirations are rightly directed, and avenues to advancement through mere good fortune are closed. These are indeed essential methods for seeking worthy men and sound rules for achieving good government. Those who govern the realm must therefore regard them as urgent priorities. How greatly men of worth and ability benefit a state! How, then, should they be encouraged and nurtured so that their abilities may be put to use? In the flourishing ages of antiquity, people were formed in harmony and nurtured in purity. They held themselves to substantial expectations and treated their own advancement with great seriousness. In these respects, they did not have to depend upon nurture through schools or selection through recommendation and examination. Since the Three Dynasties, those above have had means of seeking talent among those below, while those below have looked to those above for recognition. Yet it was through implementing the system of schools in the dang and sui districts and establishing local recommendation and selection that the Zhou also achieved good government. Our dynasty models its government on antiquity: how splendid have been the results of its employment of men!

I, an unworthy student, have long aspired to serve the world, but have had no means of making myself known. Now, prompted by your question, I venture to offer some words on the matter. In the closing years of the Zhou royal house, the regional lords no longer presented their scholars annually. Thus, although Zichan argued against demolishing the local schools, the teaching of the schools was not transmitted. After the Qin dynasty of the Ying house, men of intelligence and resourcefulness each displayed their prowess. Thus Gaozu of Han erred in neglecting the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents, and nothing was heard of instruction in schools. Considering …

title: 正德八年河南鄉試錄
text:
此則凡後世養士之不備弊可見也唐之
取士既有學館生徒州縣鄉貢矣又復別
立制舉而不專於鄉校宋之取士既有賢
良之舉進士之科矣又復增以漕試而無
考其行藝觀此則凡後世取士之未盡亦
可知也是以徇名責實之意廢敦本務實
之風微而成周良法更變已不知其幾也
祖宗設學校以教天下之士亦因成周黨庠遂
序之法而爲之爾日省之月試之而歲一
===
考之蓋以學校者教化之本源舍是將無
以責其成矣設貢舉以取天下之士亦因
成周鄉舉里選之法而行之爾舉于鄉貢
于禮部而策于
大廷蓋以貢舉者取人之正途舍是將無以
其至矣是則法之盡善固無容議其所可
言者特以學校之養固欲得人以資用也
然吏出迭入而習爲浮華進寸退尺而倖
於聲利行業已不專矣尚何望焉貢舉之
punctuated:
此則凡後世養士之不備，弊可見也。唐之取士，既有學館生徒、州縣鄉貢矣，又復別立制舉，而不專於鄉校。宋之取士，既有賢良之舉、進士之科矣，又復增以漕試，而無考其行藝。觀此，則凡後世取士之未盡，亦可知也。是以徇名責實之意廢，敦本務實之風微，而成周良法更變，已不知其幾也。
祖宗設學校以教天下之士，亦因成周黨庠遂序之法而爲之爾。日省之，月試之，而歲一考之，蓋以學校者教化之本源，舍是將無以責其成矣。設貢舉以取天下之士，亦因成周鄉舉里選之法而行之爾。舉于鄉，貢于禮部，而策于大廷，蓋以貢舉者取人之正途，舍是將無以其至矣。是則法之盡善，固無容議。其所可言者，特以學校之養，固欲得人以資用也。然吏出迭入，而習爲浮華；進寸退尺，而倖於聲利，行業已不專矣，尚何望焉？貢舉之
translation_en:
…From this, the defects arising from later ages’ inadequate cultivation of scholars can be seen. In selecting scholars, the Tang already had students of educational institutions and candidates recommended by prefectures and counties, yet it also separately established special examinations by imperial decree, rather than relying exclusively on local schools. In selecting scholars, the Song already had recommendations of the worthy and good and the jinshi examination category, yet it further added examinations administered by the Transport Commissions, without examining candidates’ conduct and learning. From this, the inadequacies of later ages’ selection of scholars can also be understood. Thus the intention of requiring actual merit to match reputation fell into disuse, the practice of strengthening fundamentals and attending to substance declined, and the excellent institutions of the Zhou at its height underwent changes beyond counting.
Our imperial ancestors established schools to educate the scholars of the realm, simply following the Zhou institutions of district and rural schools. Students are scrutinized daily, tested monthly, and examined once a year, for schools are the fountainhead of moral instruction; without them, there would be no means of holding students accountable for their achievements. The tribute examination system was established to select scholars throughout the realm, likewise following the Zhou practice of recommending men from townships and selecting them from villages. Candidates are recommended in the provinces, presented to the Ministry of Rites, and examined through policy questions at the imperial court. This is because the tribute examination system is the proper avenue for selecting men; without it, there would be no means of bringing them to attainment [?]. The perfection of these institutions thus admits of no dispute. What may be discussed is simply this: the schools’ cultivation of scholars is certainly intended to obtain men fit for service. Yet officials come and go in succession [?], while superficial display becomes habitual; advancing an inch and retreating a foot, men seek lucky gains in reputation and profit. With conduct and studies already lacking sustained commitment, what can still be hoped for? As for the tribute examination system’s…

title: 正德八年河南鄉試錄
text:
科固欲求賢以圖治也然□綺子弟得預
計偕驕惰鄙夫濫登仕籍趨向已不正矣
餘何望焉爲今之計必擇嚴毅方正之人
以居師儒之職則所養之士必端矣何至
士風之不振乎擇忠厚正直之人以居考
校之任則取士必得矣何至士習之大壞
乎雖然成天下之治者在機不在勢運天
下之機者在上不在下方今
聖天子操制作之機而賢公卿大夫又相與協
===
力于下所養所取莫非正人其所以治隆
俗美寔有望于
今日愚生菲薄而言之及此出位之罪也執事
以爲何如
第五問
同考試官教諭林　批
時務策荅者多就問目逐
句敷衍而此作獨不然他人之所詳者我畧他人之所畧者我詳
可不謂有識之士乎
尹倫
punctuated:
科固欲求賢以圖治也，然□綺子弟得預計偕，驕惰鄙夫濫登仕籍，趨向已不正矣，餘何望焉？爲今之計，必擇嚴毅方正之人以居師儒之職，則所養之士必端矣，何至士風之不振乎？擇忠厚正直之人以居考校之任，則取士必得矣，何至士習之大壞乎？雖然，成天下之治者在機不在勢，運天下之機者在上不在下。方今聖天子操制作之機，而賢公卿大夫又相與協力于下，所養所取莫非正人，其所以治隆俗美，寔有望于今日。愚生菲薄，而言之及此，出位之罪也。執事以爲何如？

第五問

同考試官教諭林批：時務策荅者，多就問目逐句敷衍，而此作獨不然。他人之所詳者我畧，他人之所畧者我詳，可不謂有識之士乎？

尹倫
translation_en:
…the examination system is certainly intended to seek worthy men in order to achieve good government. Yet sons of wealthy families [?] are allowed to join those sent to the capital for examination, while arrogant, indolent, and vulgar men improperly gain entry to the official rolls. Their aspirations are already misguided; what further hope can there be? The necessary course now is to select stern, resolute, upright men to occupy teaching posts. The scholars they nurture will then surely be principled: how could scholarly conduct fail to flourish? Select loyal, generous, honest, and upright men to serve as examiners, and the selection of scholars will surely yield the right men: how could scholarly habits fall into such grave decline?

Nevertheless, bringing good government to the realm depends upon the directing mechanism, rather than the force of circumstances; those who operate that mechanism stand above, not below. Today our sagely Son of Heaven controls the mechanism for establishing institutions, while worthy dukes, ministers, and grand masters cooperate below. Those nurtured and those selected are all upright men. There is thus real hope today for flourishing government and admirable customs. I, an ignorant student of meager worth, have nevertheless ventured to speak of these matters, thereby committing the fault of going beyond my station. What is your judgment, honored examiners?

Fifth Question

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: Most writers of policy essays on current affairs merely elaborate upon the question sentence by sentence. This composition alone does otherwise. What others discuss at length, I treat briefly; what others treat briefly, I discuss at length. Can its author not be called a man of discernment?

Yin Lun

title: 正德八年河南鄉試錄
text:
考試官學正王　批〔策問中有許多說話而此答能纂之豈謂事已往者自不必致論邪〕
考試官教授陸　批〔不爲問目所窘真策手也〕
論天下之事不可不先事而憂任天下之
事不可不先事而處論事而不知所憂必
不能得事之情任事而不知所處必不能
勝事之責不能得事之情則不足與論事
不能勝事之責則不可使任事天下之事
多矣今之論事者有能盡知所憂者乎今
===
之任事者有能盡知所處者乎而執事以
兵與食下詢承學謂時務之急非一而此
尤今日之所當議者執事寔寄憂於此不
知執事之所欲先事而處者何如諸生不
敢爲出位之思雖然亦嘗於此憂焉既承
明問敢無詞以復乎請自兵言之古者寓
兵於民三時務農一時講武六鄉之內六
軍屬焉六遂之內軍又倍焉卒有四方之
役畿內之兵不出而二伯專征諸侯共之
punctuated:
考試官學正王批〔策問中有許多說話，而此答能纂之，豈謂事已往者自不必致論邪？〕
考試官教授陸批〔不爲問目所窘，真策手也。〕
論天下之事，不可不先事而憂；任天下之事，不可不先事而處。論事而不知所憂，必不能得事之情；任事而不知所處，必不能勝事之責。不能得事之情，則不足與論事；不能勝事之責，則不可使任事。天下之事多矣，今之論事者，有能盡知所憂者乎？今之任事者，有能盡知所處者乎？而執事以兵與食下詢承學，謂時務之急非一，而此尤今日之所當議者。執事寔寄憂於此，不知執事之所欲先事而處者何如？諸生不敢爲出位之思，雖然，亦嘗於此憂焉。既承明問，敢無詞以復乎？請自兵言之。古者寓兵於民，三時務農，一時講武。六鄉之內，六軍屬焉；六遂之內，軍又倍焉。卒有四方之役，畿內之兵不出，而二伯專征，諸侯共之。
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Wang, School Director: 〔The policy question contains many points, yet this answer manages to draw them together. Does he mean that matters already past need not, of themselves, be discussed?〕
Comment by Examiner Lu, Instructor: 〔He is not constrained by the question’s individual points: truly an accomplished writer of policy essays.〕
Those who discuss the affairs of the realm must anticipate causes for concern; those who take responsibility for the affairs of the realm must make arrangements in advance. To discuss affairs without knowing what warrants concern is necessarily to fail to grasp their true circumstances; to undertake affairs without knowing how to manage them is necessarily to fail to bear the responsibilities they entail. Those who cannot grasp the true circumstances of affairs are unfit to join in discussing them; those who cannot bear their responsibilities must not be entrusted with them. The affairs of the realm are many. Among those who discuss them today, is there anyone who fully understands what warrants concern? Among those who undertake them today, is there anyone who fully understands what must be managed? You, sir, have graciously questioned us students about troops and food supplies, saying that although the urgent concerns of the day are numerous, these especially demand discussion today. These matters indeed occupy your concern, but I do not know what arrangements you wish to make in anticipation of events. We students dare not entertain thoughts that overstep our station; nevertheless, we too have felt concern about these matters. Having received your discerning question, how could I venture to offer no words in reply? Let me begin with troops. In antiquity, soldiers were drawn from among the common people: for three seasons they devoted themselves to farming, and for one season they practiced military skills. Within the six townships were assigned six armies; within the six outer districts, the number of armies was twice as great. If a campaign suddenly arose in any quarter, the troops within the royal domain did not march out. Instead, the two regional overlords exercised authority to conduct punitive expeditions, and the feudal lords jointly supported them…

title: 正德八年河南鄉試錄
text:
其或冢宰徵師不過元戎十乘爲啓行之
先耳而調兵諸侯各從其方之便不聞有
奔命之勞也諸侯之軍無王命不敢私用
其用之也所在皆蒐殺肱夾射御之士其
不用也所在皆力農桑知孝弟之民不聞
其征調之苦也請自食言之古者京畿千
里自甸服百里賦納總至於五百里米而
五百之外皆諸侯國不過任土作貢以輸
王府而賦稅米粟則未嘗徵之當時宗廟
===
百官有司之事軍旅之需千里之內賦稅
取之而自足不聞其仰餉運於畿外之諸
侯糴米粟於畿內之百姓也三年耕而餘
一年之積九年作而有三年之儲雖水旱
爲災不聞其有損瘠之民也後世井田廢
而兵民分封建罷而郡縣置舉天下之丁
夫惟上之役盡天下之賦稅惟上之供而
兵之與食視三代顧有不足之憂是必有
其故也兵之不足政失之也食之不足事
punctuated:
其或冢宰徵師，不過元戎十乘爲啓行之先耳。而調兵，諸侯各從其方之便，不聞有奔命之勞也。諸侯之軍，無王命不敢私用。其用之也，所在皆蒐殺肱夾射御之士；其不用也，所在皆力農桑、知孝弟之民，不聞其征調之苦也。
請自食言之。古者京畿千里，自甸服百里賦納總，至於五百里米，而五百之外皆諸侯國，不過任土作貢以輸王府，而賦稅米粟則未嘗徵之。當時宗廟、百官有司之事，軍旅之需，千里之內賦稅取之而自足，不聞其仰餉運於畿外之諸侯、糴米粟於畿內之百姓也。三年耕而餘一年之積，九年作而有三年之儲，雖水旱爲災，不聞其有損瘠之民也。
後世井田廢而兵民分，封建罷而郡縣置。舉天下之丁夫，惟上之役；盡天下之賦稅，惟上之供。而兵之與食，視三代顧有不足之憂，是必有其故也。兵之不足，政失之也；食之不足，事
translation_en:
…If the Minister of State on occasion summoned troops, these amounted to no more than ten great war chariots leading the advance. When troops were mobilized, each regional lord followed arrangements suited to his own territory; one hears of no exhausting rush to answer commands. Without the king’s command, the regional lords dared not deploy their armies on their own authority. When employed, the men everywhere were warriors versed in hunting and killing, “arms and flanking” [?], archery, and charioteering; when not employed, they were people devoted to farming and sericulture who understood filial piety and respect for elder brothers. One hears of no suffering caused by their conscription and mobilization.
Let me now speak of provisions. In antiquity, the royal domain extended a thousand li across. Within the royal service zone, levies ranged from grain delivered with its stalks in the first hundred li to husked grain at five hundred li. Beyond five hundred li lay the states of the regional lords, which merely supplied tribute according to the produce of their lands for delivery to the royal treasury; rice and other grain were never exacted from them as taxes. At that time, the expenses of the ancestral temples and the various officials and responsible offices, together with military requirements, were adequately met by taxes collected within the thousand-li domain. One hears of no dependence on provisions transported from regional lords outside the royal domain, or of purchases of grain from the common people within it. Three years of cultivation left a surplus sufficient for one year; nine years of work produced reserves sufficient for three. Even when floods or droughts brought disaster, one hears of no people reduced to want and emaciation.
In later ages, the well-field system was abolished, and soldiers became separated from the civilian population; enfeoffment was discontinued, and commanderies and counties were established. All the able-bodied men in the realm were at the ruler’s service, and all its taxes supplied his needs. Yet, compared with the Three Dynasties, there was instead anxiety over insufficient troops and provisions. There must have been reasons for this. Insufficient troops resulted from failures in government; insufficient provisions, from undertakings…

title: 正德八年河南鄉試錄
text:
耗之也三代無論姑舉漢事以明今日之
始末漢初南軍守宮北軍護京皆調發郡
國材官騎士分番爲之又選天下材力武
猛者以爲輕車騎士材官樓船各於其地
所宜講課武事平地用車騎山阻用材官
水泉用樓船制爲近古及光武之世都試
既罷外兵不練雖彊場之間復因外寇增
廣屯戍而國有征伐終藉京師之軍以出
自建元以及漢衰連年暴露禁旅無復鎮
===
衛之職此政之失也今之兵制能守
祖宗之法而無變焉一如漢高祖時列郡有守
有都尉都尉佐太守典武職甲卒王國則
以内史比郡守中尉比都尉侯國則亦有
相秩比令長每歲八月會太守郡尉令長
相丞咸預各以其方之所習而課殿最焉
強幹弱枝防微杜漸體統周密倖有盜賊
何假於
禁兵邊兵又土軍之調發臨時而取辦乎漢
punctuated:
耗之也。三代無論，姑舉漢事，以明今日之始末。漢初，南軍守宮，北軍護京，皆調發郡國材官、騎士，分番爲之。又選天下材力武猛者，以爲輕車、騎士、材官、樓船，各於其地所宜講課武事：平地用車騎，山阻用材官，水泉用樓船。制爲近古。及光武之世，都試既罷，外兵不練，雖彊場之間復因外寇增廣屯戍，而國有征伐，終藉京師之軍以出。自建元以及漢衰，連年暴露，禁旅無復鎮衛之職，此政之失也。
今之兵制，能守祖宗之法而無變焉，一如漢高祖時，列郡有守、有都尉，都尉佐太守典武職甲卒；王國則以内史比郡守，中尉比都尉；侯國則亦有相，秩比令長。每歲八月，會太守、郡尉、令長、相、丞，咸預，各以其方之所習而課殿最焉。強幹弱枝，防微杜漸，體統周密，倖有盜賊，何假於禁兵、邊兵，又土軍之調發，臨時而取辦乎？漢
translation_en:
…because undertakings consume it. Leaving aside the Three Dynasties, let us cite the affairs of the Han to illuminate how the present situation came about. In the early Han, the Southern Army guarded the palace and the Northern Army protected the capital. Both were staffed by infantrymen and cavalrymen levied from the commanderies and kingdoms to serve in rotation. Men of strength, ability, and martial prowess were also selected throughout the empire to serve in light chariot units, cavalry, infantry, and tower-ship forces. Each practiced and was tested in military skills suited to the local terrain: chariots and cavalry were used on level ground, infantry in rugged mountains, and tower ships on waterways. This system closely resembled that of antiquity. By the reign of Guangwu, however, the general military reviews had been abolished, and troops outside the capital were no longer trained. Although garrisons along the frontiers were expanded in response to foreign incursions, whenever the state undertook a campaign it ultimately relied on troops dispatched from the capital. From the Jianyuan era [?] down to the decline of the Han, the imperial guards remained exposed in the field year after year and no longer fulfilled their function of securing and protecting the capital. This was a failure of governance.
If the present military system could preserve the laws of our imperial ancestors without alteration, just as in the time of Han Gaozu, each commandery would have an Administrator and a Commandant, with the Commandant assisting the Administrator in managing military offices and armed troops. In the kingdoms, the Chamberlain for the Capital would correspond to a commandery Administrator, and the Commandant of the Capital to a commandery Commandant. The marquisates would likewise have Chancellors, ranked on a par with county Magistrates and Chiefs. In the eighth month of every year, the Administrators, commandery Commandants, county Magistrates and Chiefs, Chancellors, and Assistant Magistrates would assemble and all take part, assessing performance from worst to best according to the skills practiced in each region. With the trunk strengthened and the branches weakened, trouble checked at its slightest beginnings and prevented from developing, and the structure of authority comprehensive and closely ordered, should bandits happen to arise, what need would there be to levy imperial guards, frontier troops, or local troops and hastily make arrangements as the occasion arose? In the Han…

title: 正德八年河南鄉試錄
text:
文帝時封國漸衆諸侯王自食其地王府
所入蓋寡又與匈奴和親歲致金繒後數
爲邊患天子親將出擊復因河決有築塞
勞費大司農財用宜不致充溢而文帝在
位十二年即賜民田租次年遂除之粟陳
貫朽以貽武帝之世乃外事四夷內興土
功用度不足遂募民入奴婢得以終身復
及入羊爲郎又令民買爵置武功爵造皮
幣白金置鹽鐵均輸官筭商車緡錢榷酒
===
酤卒之盜賊蠭起而有輪臺之悔此事之
耗也今之賦稅能守
祖宗之法而無變焉一如漢文帝時恭儉在上
百金之費亦不苟用宮闈是儆流傳國都
莫有奢侈之習海內富庶家給人足天下
之治清和咸理自無他變萬一不虞何暇
於
內帑邊儲之借與輸納銀粟之令當事而會
計乎若夫執事所謂壯丁之增今無事之
punctuated:
文帝時，封國漸衆，諸侯王自食其地，王府所入蓋寡。又與匈奴和親，歲致金繒，後數爲邊患，天子親將出擊。復因河決，有築塞勞費，大司農財用宜不致充溢。而文帝在位十二年，即賜民田租，次年遂除之。粟陳貫朽，以貽武帝之世，乃外事四夷，內興土功，用度不足，遂募民入奴婢，得以終身復；及入羊爲郎，又令民買爵，置武功爵，造皮幣白金，置鹽鐵均輸官，筭商車緡錢，榷酒酤。卒之盜賊蠭起，而有輪臺之悔，此事之耗也。
今之賦稅，能守祖宗之法而無變焉，一如漢文帝時，恭儉在上，百金之費亦不苟用，宮闈是儆，流傳國都，莫有奢侈之習。海內富庶，家給人足，天下之治，清和咸理，自無他變。萬一不虞，何暇於內帑邊儲之借與輸納銀粟之令，當事而會計乎？
若夫執事所謂壯丁之增，今無事之
translation_en:
…In Emperor Wen’s time, the number of enfeoffed kingdoms gradually increased. The feudatory kings drew their revenues directly from their own territories, so receipts into the royal treasury were presumably meager. Moreover, peace through marriage alliances was concluded with the Xiongnu, and gold and silk were sent to them annually. Subsequently they repeatedly troubled the frontier, and the emperor personally led troops out against them. Breaches of the Yellow River also entailed labor and expenditure on building embankments and closing the breaches. The financial resources of the Chamberlain for the National Treasury could hardly have been overflowing. Yet in the twelfth year of his reign, Emperor Wen remitted the people’s land tax, and in the following year abolished it altogether. Grain grew old in the granaries, and the strings holding the cash rotted away: such was the wealth bequeathed to Emperor Wu’s age. Then campaigns were undertaken against the barbarians of the four quarters abroad, and construction projects were launched at home. When funds proved insufficient, people were invited to surrender male and female slaves in return for lifelong exemption from service obligations; they could also present sheep to become court gentlemen [?]. People were further allowed to purchase ranks of nobility; ranks for military merit were instituted; leather currency and “white metal” currency were manufactured; officials were appointed for salt, iron, and equitable transport; taxes were levied on merchants’ carts and strings of cash; and a monopoly was imposed on the sale of liquor. In the end, bandits arose in swarms, and there came the repentance expressed at Luntai. Such was the depletion caused by these undertakings.
If taxation today can adhere to the laws of the ancestral emperors without alteration, following precisely the example of Emperor Wen of Han, with reverence and frugality practiced by the ruler, even an expense of a hundred units of gold would not be incurred carelessly. The palace would be admonished accordingly, and this influence would spread through the capital, leaving no habits of extravagance. All within the seas would be prosperous, every household adequately provided for, and every person supplied with enough. The realm would be governed with clarity and harmony, and everything would be in order; naturally, no other disturbances would arise. Should something unforeseen nevertheless occur, what time would there be, once the emergency was upon us, to make financial calculations about borrowing from the imperial privy treasury and frontier reserves, or issuing orders for contributions of silver and grain?
As for the increase in able-bodied men that you, sir, have proposed, now, in a time of peace …

title: 正德八年河南鄉試錄
text:
時籍其人而團結教集必將廢其生理而
又使之自備器械自齎食用必有所不能
辦將以食于官則官亦不給將以免其正
差則均徭之在所司紛如牛毛又將移之
誰乎吏姦黠者與之為市家至戶到追胥
迫脅錄放之間害民滋益多而事終無所
濟若彼民壯令甲所著當免義丁以貼助
其役今有司審編中間丁單力弱無所仰
給不能自脫者亦多矣終歲奔走豈專為
===
城守計貪冒之徒又從而科削之為今之
計州縣獨可照額選補民壯精健勇敢務
足其數倣宋弓箭社槍仗手管操官員以
時教習驗覆等第致其賞罰凡例所應優
免有糧免糧有丁免丁以惠恤之大州縣
蓋數百人小縣亦百十餘人緩急遣用豈
不亦可助戎行之不足邪屯地之清河南
民俗方健此訟始因年儉棄賣祖業漂流
異鄉經涉數代歸還廬井鄰里非舊桑榆
punctuated:
時，籍其人而團結教集，必將廢其生理，而又使之自備器械，自齎食用，必有所不能辦。將以食于官，則官亦不給；將以免其正差，則均徭之在所司紛如牛毛，又將移之誰乎？吏姦黠者與之為市，家至戶到，追胥迫脅，錄放之間，害民滋益多，而事終無所濟。若彼民壯，令甲所著，當免義丁以貼助其役。今有司審編，中間丁單力弱、無所仰給、不能自脫者亦多矣。終歲奔走，豈專為城守計？貪冒之徒，又從而科削之。為今之計，州縣獨可照額選補民壯，精健勇敢，務足其數。倣宋弓箭社、槍仗手，管操官員以時教習，驗覆等第，致其賞罰。凡例所應優免，有糧免糧，有丁免丁，以惠恤之。大州縣蓋數百人，小縣亦百十餘人，緩急遣用，豈不亦可助戎行之不足邪？
屯地之清，河南民俗方健，此訟始因年儉，棄賣祖業，漂流異鄉，經涉數代，歸還廬井，鄰里非舊，桑榆
translation_en:
…in such times, registering these men and organizing them into units for training would inevitably disrupt their livelihoods. If they were also required to provide their own weapons and bring their own provisions, some would certainly be unable to afford it. If the government were to feed them, its resources would likewise be insufficient. If they were exempted from their regular service obligations, the equitable-service levies administered by the authorities are already as numerous and tangled as ox hairs: to whom would those obligations then be transferred? Cunning clerks would make a business of this, going from house to house, pursuing and coercing people. In enrolling some and releasing others, they would inflict ever greater harm on the people, while ultimately accomplishing nothing.
As for the local militiamen, the statutes expressly provide that auxiliary men serving as yiding should receive exemptions so that they can help support the militiamen’s service. Yet among those now assessed and enrolled by the local authorities, many belong to households with few adult males and meager resources, have no means of support, and cannot extricate themselves. They hurry about on service throughout the year: is this solely for the defense of the city? Greedy and corrupt men then impose further exactions upon them.
Under present circumstances, prefectures and counties should simply select and replace local militiamen according to the established quotas, choosing sturdy, vigorous, and courageous men and ensuring that the full numbers are maintained. Following the examples of the Song archery associations and spearmen, officers responsible for drill should train them at regular intervals, inspect and grade them, and administer rewards and punishments accordingly. Wherever the regulations allow preferential exemptions, those liable for grain payments should be exempted from them, and those liable for service by adult males should be exempted from that service, thus giving them relief and support. Large prefectures and counties would have several hundred men, and even small counties a hundred or somewhat more. Deployed when needed, could they not help make up deficiencies in the ranks of the troops?
As for clarifying the status of military agricultural lands, the people of Henan are currently vigorous in litigation [?]. These disputes originally arose when, in years of poor harvests, people abandoned or sold their ancestral property and wandered to other regions. After several generations, they returned to their homes and holdings, but their neighbors were no longer the same, and the mulberry and elm trees…

title: 正德八年河南鄉試錄
text:
叚植年歲既久易生假冒遠認死亡之族
旁引親舊之人或許水退地出或稱産去
稅存孰官孰私莫可取據良疇委而不開
柔桑枯而不採寔由經界未正故也愚以
爲所爭之地宜限年斷事久難明悉屬今
主亦息訟之一端若夫積稅額之舊逋蓋
不係此今各州縣民戶有有稅無田者有
有田無稅者或緣侵耕失稅或推割不行
或兵火後稅籍不存彼此求脫或詭名寄
===
産或逃戶遺稅逃田積稅人得推託負責
本里藏情隱姦致爭非一有司能就本里
以無田之稅均增於原額之田無稅之田
減均於原額之稅入已稱善不知減均得
偏輕之利而均增得偏重之害也爲今之
計宜依朱子漳州經界奏札推擇官吏委
任責成步筭畝數攢造圖帳費從官出隨
産均稅特許過鄉通戶均紐麻錢百里之
內輕重齊同一邑行之既協人情移之他
punctuated:
叚植，年歲既久，易生假冒，遠認死亡之族，旁引親舊之人，或許水退地出，或稱産去稅存，孰官孰私，莫可取據。良疇委而不開，柔桑枯而不採，寔由經界未正故也。愚以爲所爭之地，宜限年斷；事久難明，悉屬今主，亦息訟之一端。若夫積稅額之舊逋，蓋不係此。

今各州縣民戶，有有稅無田者，有有田無稅者，或緣侵耕失稅，或推割不行，或兵火後稅籍不存，彼此求脫，或詭名寄産，或逃戶遺稅、逃田積稅，人得推託，負責本里，藏情隱姦，致爭非一。有司能就本里，以無田之稅均增於原額之田，無稅之田減均於原額之稅，入已稱善。不知減均得偏輕之利，而均增得偏重之害也。爲今之計，宜依朱子《漳州經界奏札》，推擇官吏，委任責成，步筭畝數，攢造圖帳，費從官出，隨産均稅，特許過鄉通戶，均紐麻錢，百里之內，輕重齊同。一邑行之，既協人情，移之他
translation_en:
…planted [?]. After so many years, fraudulent claims readily arise: people claim distant kinship with deceased families and invoke collateral connections with relatives and old acquaintances. Some assert that land emerged when the waters receded; others say that their property is gone but its taxes remain. Which land is public and which private cannot be established from any reliable evidence. Good fields lie abandoned and untilled; tender mulberry trees wither without their leaves being gathered. This is truly because the land boundaries have not been properly determined. In my humble opinion, disputed land should be adjudicated according to a limit on how far back claims may reach. Where matters are too old to establish clearly, the land should all belong to its present holders. This, too, is one means of ending litigation. As for old arrears of assessed taxes, these are a separate matter.

Among the households of the various subprefectures and counties today, some owe taxes but have no fields, while others have fields but owe no taxes. This may result from encroaching cultivation that escapes taxation, or from failure to transfer the tax liability when land changes hands. Sometimes tax registers have been lost through warfare, and each party seeks to evade liability. Some lodge property under fictitious names; in other cases, fleeing households leave taxes unpaid, or taxes accumulate on abandoned fields. People are thus able to evade responsibility and shift the burden onto their own village. Concealment of the facts and fraudulent dealings give rise to disputes in many ways. If the responsible officials can work within the village, distributing the taxes for which there is no corresponding land as additions to the fields already assessed, and incorporating untaxed fields so as to reduce and redistribute the existing tax assessment, this is already considered good administration [?]. They do not realize that the reduction and redistribution confer the advantage of an unduly light burden, while the additional distribution imposes the harm of an unduly heavy one.

The appropriate course now is to follow Master Zhu’s Memorial on the Land Survey in Zhangzhou: select officials and clerks, entrust them with the work, and hold them responsible for its completion. They should measure and calculate the acreage in mu and compile maps and registers, with the expenses paid from public funds. Taxes should be apportioned equitably according to property, with special permission to cross township boundaries and include households in a common assessment, equalizing the assessment of hemp money [?], so that the burden is uniform throughout the hundred-li area. Once this has been implemented in one county and accords with the people’s wishes, it can be extended to other…

title: 正德八年河南鄉試錄
text:
郡當無不可行者然行之詳則足爲一定
之法行之略則適生他日之弊此責成之
要得人也執事之所憂而所欲處者豈止
是而已乎民壯田稅在執事處之易易耳
兵食之大者廟堂之議必將以入告于吾
聖天子易傳有之節以制度不傷財不害民不
傷財則不害民矣不傷財則足食而不害
民則足兵矣宋人黄紙放白紙催行於赦
令之餘初刺手繼刺面見於赦榜之後然
則孔子所謂足兵民信之者獨何歟謹對
punctuated: 郡，當無不可行者。然行之詳，則足爲一定之法；行之略，則適生他日之弊。此責成之要，得人也。執事之所憂而所欲處者，豈止是而已乎？民壯、田稅，在執事處之易易耳。兵食之大者，廟堂之議必將以入告于吾聖天子。《易傳》有之：「節以制度，不傷財，不害民。」不傷財則不害民矣；不傷財則足食，而不害民則足兵矣。宋人「黄紙放，白紙催」，行於赦令之餘；「初刺手，繼刺面」，見於赦榜之後。然則孔子所謂「足兵，民信之」者，獨何歟？謹對。
translation_en:
…in other prefectures, there should be nowhere that it cannot be implemented. Yet if implemented thoroughly, it can serve as a settled rule; if implemented cursorily, it will merely breed abuses in days to come. The key to assigning responsibility for its accomplishment is to obtain the right people. Surely these are not the only matters that concern you and that you wish to address? Local militiamen and land taxes are readily dealt with by you. On the larger matters of military provision and food supplies, the court’s deliberations will surely be submitted to our sage Son of Heaven.

The Commentary on the Book of Changes says: “Regulate through institutions and measures, without damaging resources or harming the people.” If resources are not damaged, the people will not be harmed. Preserving resources ensures sufficient food; sparing the people harm ensures sufficient military provision. Under the Song, “yellow paper remitted, white paper pressed for payment”—this occurred even after decrees of amnesty; “first they tattooed the hands, then they tattooed the faces”—this was seen even after amnesty proclamations. What, then, becomes of Confucius’s words, “sufficient military provision” and “the people’s trust”? Respectfully submitted in reply.

title: 正德八年河南鄉試錄
text:
河南鄉試錄後序
論學術於三代之後者必以
宋爲上漢次之唐爲下夫漢
唐所以不及宋者非其文不
足也特所務者文焉而已矣
有宋眞儒繼作而堯舜禹湯
文武周孔千載不傳之緒賴
===
以復明士生斯時幸矣然自
以朋黨斥以僞學乃使道學
之名爲世大禁而眞儒之用
不獲盡展此寔幸中之不幸
者我
祖宗創業垂統
聖子神孫嗣守鴻圖百五十年
punctuated:
河南鄉試錄後序

論學術於三代之後者，必以宋爲上，漢次之，唐爲下。夫漢唐所以不及宋者，非其文不足也，特所務者文焉而已矣。有宋眞儒繼作，而堯舜禹湯文武周孔千載不傳之緒，賴以復明。士生斯時，幸矣。然自以朋黨斥，以僞學，乃使道學之名爲世大禁，而眞儒之用不獲盡展，此寔幸中之不幸者。我祖宗創業垂統，聖子神孫嗣守鴻圖百五十年，
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Henan Provincial Examination

Those who discuss learning after the Three Dynasties invariably rank the Song highest, the Han next, and the Tang lowest. The reason the Han and Tang fell short of the Song was not that their literary accomplishments were insufficient, but simply that literature alone was their concern. Under the Song, true Confucian scholars arose in succession, and through them the tradition of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, Wu, the Duke of Zhou, and Confucius, which had gone untransmitted for a thousand years, was brought to light again. Scholars born in that age were fortunate indeed. Yet once these scholars were denounced as a faction and their learning condemned as false [?], the very name of Learning of the Way became a great taboo throughout the realm, and true Confucian scholars could not fully put their abilities into practice. This was indeed misfortune amid good fortune. Our imperial ancestors founded the dynasty and handed down its succession; their sagely sons and divine grandsons have inherited and preserved this grand imperial enterprise for a hundred and fifty years…

title: 正德八年河南鄉試錄
text:
茲一惟敦尚名教尊崇正學
人非堯舜禹湯文武周孔之
書不讀學非堯舜禹湯文武
周孔之道不用以故士之所
業粹然歸於純正殆復過于
宋馬漢唐無論也正德癸酉
秋河南例當開科取士凡執
===
事者咸祗若
國家盛典矢心殫力莫敢怠遑
振作士類視昔有加而所取
士有限者遵
定制爾錄既成學夔濫竽考校
之末宜序諸末簡噫士不幸
生不逢時猶當違俗以強學
punctuated:
茲，一惟敦尚名教，尊崇正學。人非堯舜禹湯文武周孔之書不讀，學非堯舜禹湯文武周孔之道不用。以故士之所業，粹然歸於純正，殆復過于宋馬，漢唐無論也。
正德癸酉秋，河南例當開科取士。凡執事者，咸祗若國家盛典，矢心殫力，莫敢怠遑。振作士類，視昔有加，而所取士有限者，遵定制爾。
錄既成，學夔濫竽考校之末，宜序諸末簡。噫！士不幸生不逢時，猶當違俗以強學。
translation_en:
…down to the present, consistently esteeming moral teaching and honoring orthodox learning. People read only the writings of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, Wu, Zhou, and Kong; in their learning they apply only the Way of these sages. Thus the studies pursued by scholars have become thoroughly pure and orthodox, perhaps even surpassing those of the Song [?]; the Han and Tang need not be discussed.
In the autumn of the guiyou year of Zhengde [1513], Henan was due, according to established practice, to hold the examination and select scholars. All those charged with its conduct reverently observed this grand institution of the state, pledging their resolve and exhausting their strength, none daring to slacken or take their ease. Their efforts to inspire the scholars exceeded those of earlier times; the number selected was limited only because they followed the prescribed regulations.
Now that the record is complete, I, Xuekui, having undeservedly occupied a place among the lowest ranks of the examiners, ought to write a concluding preface on its final leaves. Alas! Even scholars unfortunate enough to be born in an unfavorable age should resist prevailing customs and strive diligently in their studies…

title: 正德八年河南鄉試錄
text:
冒禁以成身今河南爲萬古
斯文所發之源爲宋程氏兩
夫子所出之地而况接壤
帝畿風化之所漸涵者最先且盛
諸士子幸而生于其鄉又幸
而遭逢其時兹乃賓興而來
隨計而往嚮用高遠此其權
===
輿要皆慎始慎終正已正物
相與嚮成
太平熙洽之治於億萬年也大
抵科目取士雖以文而主司
所望乎士者不徒以文士之
進身雖以科目而所以自成
其身者不可徒恃乎科目設
punctuated:
冒禁以成身。今河南爲萬古斯文所發之源，爲宋程氏兩夫子所出之地，而况接壤帝畿，風化之所漸涵者最先且盛。諸士子幸而生于其鄉，又幸而遭逢其時，兹乃賓興而來，隨計而往，嚮用高遠，此其權輿。要皆慎始慎終，正已正物，相與嚮成太平熙洽之治於億萬年也。
大抵科目取士雖以文，而主司所望乎士者不徒以文；士之進身雖以科目，而所以自成其身者不可徒恃乎科目。設
translation_en:
…and brave prohibitions to perfect themselves. Now Henan is the source from which this cultural tradition has issued for all ages, and the land that produced the two Masters Cheng of the Song dynasty. Moreover, it borders the imperial capital region, and has received the transforming influence of moral instruction earlier and more abundantly than other places. These scholars are fortunate to have been born in this land, and fortunate also to have encountered this age. They now come forward through the ceremonial selection of worthy men and go on to the capital with the provincial tribute delegation. Their prospects for employment are lofty and far-reaching; this is their beginning. Above all, they must exercise care from beginning to end, rectify themselves and others, and together help bring about an age of great peace, prosperity, and harmony lasting countless ages.
In general, although the examinations select scholars through their writing, those presiding over them expect more from scholars than writing alone. Although scholars advance through the examinations, they cannot rely solely on the examinations to perfect themselves. If…
